overview:
Welcome to I.S. 235, Academy for New Americans! As a Citywide program in District 30, we create an inclusive environment where every student is seen, heard, and celebrated. Our mission is to equip students to lead with excellence. We serve newly arrived students and aspiring global leaders in grades 6-8, providing a nurturing space for academic achievement, creativity, and growth.
Our approach includes comprehensive language support through Spanish Dual Language (DL), English as a New Language (ENL), Transitional Bilingual Education (TBE), and support for Students with Interrupted Formal Education (SIFE)ensuring effective acquisition and academic success.
Enrichment includes S.T.E.A.M, Robotics, Hydroponics, World Language (HS credit), and Financial Literacy. Arts integration is supported by partnerships with the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music, Lincoln Center, Artist Year, ArtsConnection, Urban Advantage, Behind the Book, Queens C.A.S.A., and NY Edge.
Community engagement is key. Students enjoy field trips to universities, museums, and cultural sites, alongside science fairs and service projects that instill civic responsibility.
Student agency is central. Through our Student Leadership Ambassador Program, learners become confident leaders. SEL-infused practices and counseling ensure students are emotionally and socially supported.
Our Parent Partnership Program fosters strong family ties via workshops, events, and multilingual resources to keep families informed.
At I.S. 235, potential is discovered, nurtured, and realized. Join us in shaping futures and opening doors to lifelong success.

overview: Young Writers is a small, supportive 6-12 school community where excellent teaching, close relationships, and high expectations lead students to secondary and post secondary success. Our Summer Bridge program allows students to connect with current staff, build relationships with other incoming peers, and engage in activities that will help them be successful in their first year. We use a restorative approach to support student development, strengthen relationships and as an alternative to traditional discipline. Classes are student-centered and focus on developing reading, writing, discussion, and presentation skills. Our academic rigor is supported by academic intervention services built into student's schedules. We believe that young people should be provided with the space to explore their identity, the tools to advocate for themselves, and the skills to achieve on their path to college and career. Students are exposed to possible college and career paths through virtual and in-person college trips. Along with college trips, students are able to engage with guest speakers from various career backgrounds throughout the school year. Our 6th graders will end the year as a contributing author to a published book through various publishing companies. As a 6-12 school our 8th grade middle school students are guaranteed admission to our competitive high school.

overview: Arts and Letters 305 United has three guiding principles that are woven throughout all aspects of our school. They are student voice, compassion and curiosity, and equity and antiracism. Middle school students start each day with a 6-8 grade morning meeting in which they get the opportunity to connect with their teachers, classmates, and themselves to set them up for a successful day. Other aspects of our school community include advisory, electives, roundtables, and strong arts instruction. Each grade goes on an overnight trip that is connected to their content learning. Our strong school culture is built on engaging academic and social emotional content, restorative justice practices, and the belief that joy and justice are at the heart of everything we do.

overview: At ACCION Academy, we have a unique opportunity to provide an individualized, warm, and caring environment for our students because our school is just the right size. This means that our highly motivated and compassionate teachers can form meaningful relationships with students and parents on the journey towards success. We can give each child our full attention to ensure they receive whatever services, programs, or activities they need to grow. Academically, we strive to provide our students with ample opportunities to reach their full potential. We currently offer Algebra 1 Regents course and we are looking to add more courses in the coming year. ACCION stands for "Achievement, Community, Consciousness, Integrity, Opportunity Now!" Our family-oriented school community fosters the highest levels of achievement, mentoring, and service. The student government helps to influence our school's decisions. Our CBO, Replications, provides additional supports in mental health, academic tutoring and attendance. Our after-school program SONYC, through Eastside House, provides enrichment and recreational activities to promote student autonomy and hands on activity through role play and problem solving. They also foment leadership skills within our students and provide the opportunity to attend a week leadership retreat in Washington DC where students engage in activities to Furthermore, there are variety of activities including Basketball Team, Chess Club, Drama Club, Volleyball Club, Student Government, Dance Club, PGC and Beyond Differences Accelerators (Social Emotional) and much more.

overview: At I.S. 126, we are committed to creating a safe and inspiring learning environment that empowers students to reach their highest potential. Our rigorous curriculum, aligned with the Common Core Learning Standards (CCLS), encourages critical thinking, collaboration, and prepares students for success in an evolving world. We go beyond traditional academics by offering college readiness programs, including classes for the Specialized High School Admissions Test (SHSAT) and New York State Exams, ensuring our students are not just prepared for high school but set up for long-term success. As a proud member of the National Honor Society, I.S. 126 fosters a dynamic environment where students are encouraged to do their best and unlock their full potential. Our strong partnership with Zone 126 helps students develop academic, leadership, and social-emotional skills, ensuring they grow as well-rounded individuals prepared to lead in their communities. At I.S. 126, we believe in sparking curiosity and creativity through arts residencies, daily access to Chromebooks, laptops, and Smart Boards, and state-of-the-art Science and Computer Labs. Our Hydroponics Lab provides hands-on learning that connects students with nature. We recognize that collaboration between school and home is vital for student success. We maintain an open-door policy, inviting parents to be active partners in their children's education. Additionally, bus service for eligible 6th graders ensures transportation is never a barrier to learning. At I.S. 126, we are more than just a schoolwe are a community of dedicated educators, students, and families, united in our mission to help every child thrive.

overview: I.S. 240 Magnet School of STE(a+)M is a diverse middle school (grades 6-8) serving approximately 400 students who speak over 10 languages. Our vision,Building a Better World, is realized through Global Awareness, Critical Consciousness, and Project-Based Learning on a digital platform. As a Magnet school, we offer a specialized curriculum in Technology, Engineering, Foreign Language, and the Arts, alongside core subjects like ELA, Math, Science, and Social Studies. Our science program follows the SCALES curriculum and is enriched by partnerships with NYU Tandon, PACE University, Kingsborough Community College, Midwood High School, Girl Be Heard, Broadway Junior, and CAMBA. Students engage in real-world learning through our Innovation Lab (Robotics, 3D Printing, Computer Tech), Hydroponic Lab, and Outdoor Garden. For advanced learners, our Polaris Bridge Program connects Andries Hudde MS students with Midwood HS, offering accelerated STEM courses and SHSAT prep. While not guaranteeing admission, Polaris builds a strong foundation for success in specialized high schools. To support social-emotional wellness, we partner with Mindful SEAD and School Culture Solutions, fostering identity awareness, empathy, and global understanding. We celebrate student voice and achievement through events like STOP Bullying Day, SEL Day, PBL Expos, Science Fair, Civics Day, and more. Our after-school programs include Broadway Junior, STEP at Kingsborough, CAMBA, Girl Be Heard, academic support, and Title III ENL services. In Fall 2025, we ll launch new student interest clubs.

overview:
Antonia Pantoja Preparatory Academy is a school for leadership. We are a New York City public school for students in grades six to twelve dedicated to supporting students to become active, college-ready leaders of their community in the spirit of Dr. Pantoja. Our test scores are consistently above the district average -- last year they were the highest in the neighborhood! We are a small school and get to know every student well and support their needs and growth. Class sizes are never more than 22 in a room. Our school is unique. Students that enter the sixth grade may remain with us in their high school years before moving own to college or a career. While few 6th graders are thinking about life after high school, APPA is already preparing them for it.Through this long-term journey, our students and their families form strong bonds and relationships with staff that create a sense of belonging, support, and scholarship.
In high school, students have the opportunity to take college classes beginning in their sophomore year.All upperclassmen take rich full-time internships in the real-world, working in hospitals, law offices, and other career-expanding locations. Come join us!Our dynamic community is the best school for students looking for a small community where they will be known, challenged, and supported.

overview: Archimedes Academy is a mission-driven 6-12 community dedicated to ensuring our students graduate as strategic advocates equipped for sustaining careers and long-term economic mobility. Our Math & Science-focused curriculum serves as a dynamic launchpad, blending rigorous AP courseworkincluding AP Statistics, US History, Literature, and Psychology with the ability to earn up to 12 free college credits through our College Now program. We cultivate real-world expertise through immersive pathways in robotics, cybersecurity, drone piloting, and computer science, bolstered by industry partnerships with organizations like Omni Learn and NY Sun Works. Beyond academics, we nurture the whole child through a robust arts program featuring dance residencies and Broadway excursions, alongside hands-on learning in our campus hydroponics lab and global service-learning through Build On. With personalized one-on-one counseling, comprehensive advisory support, vibrant after-school programming via Omni learn, and competitive PSAL/CHAMPS athletics, we provide a technology-rich, deeply connected environment where every student is challenged, supported, and ready to thrive.

overview: Founded in September 2002, the Baccalaureate School for Global Education (BSGE) provides a world-class educational experience aligned with the frameworks and standards of the International Baccalaureate Program. We expect all students who successfully complete our course of study to be prepared for the International Baccalaureate diploma. The International Baccalaureate Program is a rigorous college preparatory course of study that meets the needs of highly motivated secondary school students. The IB diploma allows graduates to fulfill requirements of national education systems worldwide, incorporating the best elements of each. Our student body is composed of an ethnically diverse and economically varied population of young people from different neighborhoods in Queens, including Jamaica, Forest Hills, Corona, Astoria, Woodside, Laurelton, Rosedale, Far Rockaway, Queens Village, Hollis, Richmond Hill, Middle Village, South Ozone, Jackson Heights, Rego Park and Long Island City.Located in Astoria, BSGE students learn in an environment that encourages inquiry, as well as intellectual and social development with a commitment to human responsibility and social justice.

overview: Ballet Tech, The NYC Public School for Dance, provides students in grades 4-8 with a high quality academic education and rigorous classical dance training. The school is a unique partnership between the NYC Department of Education and Ballet Tech Foundation, which provides dance instruction. At Ballet Tech, we believe that students learn best in a supportive and positive environment that encourages discussion and requires critical thinking. Ballet Tech's middle school builds on the academic foundation established in its elementary school, raising the level of intellectual rigor while also addressing the social and emotional needs unique to middle school students. Middle school students take dance classes 5 days a week. The core middle school dance curriculum includes classes in ballet technique, pointe, allegro, and modern. In addition, students take supporting dance classes such as audition prep, jazz, and tap. "Kids Dance," Ballet Tech's student performance troupe, provides students with the opportunity to learn choreography and develop performance skills. Kids Dance performs annually at The Joyce Theater in Chelsea, where it presents programs for families and young audiences.

overview: We transform the middle school journey into a high-energy launchpad for future changemakers, framing student growth around academic excellence and social justice leadership From day one, students are embraced as true leaders who take charge of their responsibilities through our PACT core valuesPersistence, Accountability, Communication, and Teamwork. This leadership mindset fuels our campus-wide competition, where students earn PACT Points for their House by proving their academic success, winning uniform points, and hitting attendance goals, all leading to live weekly standings, custom school parties, and epic celebration excursions every semester. Our leaders actively steer their own education by maintaining a personalized Promotion Portfolio that showcases concrete evidence of their learning, and they regularly lead their own peer discussions during interactive community circles and one-on-one Learning Conferences with teachers. Every student is assigned to a small family group to make sure they receive the adult support and attention necessary for success. Combined with our robust athletic programs and creative outlets like instrumental music, chorus, band, robotics, media production, and fabulous, completely free field trips, we ensure that striving for big academic expectations goes hand-in-hand with an incredibly fun, supportive, and active school community.

overview: Bronx Dance Academy is a high-achieving performing arts middle school focused on supporting students artistically, academically, and socially. BDA geniuses consistently perform above the district and city averages on assessments due to the strong core instruction they receive. In addition, students learn to channel and develop their own unique interests, creativity, and passion though the performing and visual arts. Thanks to the small, friendly school environment, BDA students form meaningful relationships with mentors who support students through the many changes that come with being a middle school student. BDA offers two majors, Dance or Visual Arts. Students must always audition for a spot at BDA before being admitted to their major program. Auditions take place in-person at the school or electronically through MySchools. Once students are selected for BDA, they master different art forms and are taken to a variety of trips each school year to places like the American Ballet Theatre, Alvin Ailey Dance Company, art museums, colleges, theme parks, and more. In addition, the MMCC afterschool program runs everyday from 2:50 - 5:45pm and nurtures student's understanding of theatre, drama, choir, music, videography and production, cooking, kickboxing, school newspaper. BDA also offers BDA Academic Success program for after-school small-group tutoring, and BDA Saturday Program for targeted instruction,BDA is a place where young artists can develop their knowledge and skills to reach their true potential for genius.

overview:
Bronx Park Middle School is a welcoming, academically ambitious community where students think critically, lead with purpose, and grow as independent learners. As an IB Middle Years Programme school, we provide inquiry-based learning experiences that connect classroom content to real-world issues and develop knowledgeable, reflective, and compassionate global citizens. Students engage daily with rigorous literacy, math, science, and social studies instruction using high-quality, research-backed materialsincluding EL Education and Illustrative Mathematics. Through school-wide inquiry, students explore meaningful questions, analyze evidence, and apply learning to authentic challenges. Every student participates in Advisory, where they build relationships, develop leadership, and embody our PRIDE values: Presence, Reflection, Innovation, Determination, and Empathy. Our culture centers on social-emotional safety and restorative practices so every student feels known and ready to learn.
Bronx Park is open-enrollment no test, no audition, no lottery. We proudly serve a diverse community, including English Language Learners and students with IEPs, with specialized support woven into every part of the day. Enrichment opportunities include multiple regents, coding, robotics, arts, athletics, and student government. Through the IB MYP Community Project, students in every grade engage in self-directed service learning - identifying a community need and designing a real response. Our mission: "Flow. Growth. Purpose. Every Student, Every Day" reflects our belief that students thrive when supported, stretched, and connected to purpose. Our students have achieved all-time highs in NYS ELA and Math proficiency, proof that high expectations and genuine care go hand in hand.

overview: Brooklyn Collaborative is committed to developing students and staff who are kind, openminded, persistent, responsible, and courageous. Our students and our curriculum reflect the city we live in. We are committed to being diverse with regard to race, ethnicity, socio-economics, religion, and academics. Our students see themselves and their communities represented widely in the history they study, the books and texts they read, and the expeditions they engage in. Our students use the city as their classroom. Fieldwork is a regular part of learning at Brooklyn Collaborative: students regularly meet with experts, tour neighborhoods and museums, analyze artifacts, collect lab samples, and more. We are committed to developing the social and emotional self as well as the academic self through Crew. In crew (a daily advisory class), students learn to be agents of self-change, to take responsibility for their learning, and to develop supportive relationships with adults and peers. We are a Grades 6-12 school with a 100% college acceptance rate and a NYS Regents waiver. Our major partners are NYC Outward Bound and the New York Performance Standards Consortium.There's something for everyone at BCS!

overview: The Brooklyn School of Inquiry programs are designed to foster self-directed learning by encouraging exploration, inquiry and reflective thinking. We are a K-8, citywide gifted and talented school, rooted in the principles of inquiry-based learning and progressive education. We emphasize STEAM education, literacy development, play-based learning and social and emotional development. The 2017-2018 school year marked the beginning of the Diversity in Admissions program and 40% of our incoming kindergarten class is eligible for free or reduced price lunch. We are not a zoned, community school and 85% of our students are bussed to the school by either the Office of Pupil Transportation or private busses that are funded by the families that use them. We are deeply committed to a strong sense of community rooted in the Tribes Agreements, Responsive Classroom approaches and our middle school advisory program. We feel strongly that student choice allows for positive growth and development, therefore during the school day, we offer lunch clubs, elective courses and our students engage in a variety of after school programs such as debate, band, robotics, musical theater and art and math clubs. We have a state-of-the-art rooftop STEM lab where all students study hydroponics, aquaponics and other environmental science topics.

overview: The Brooklyn Science and Engineering Academy (BSEA) promotes a family-like environment with small class sizes, open communication with families and interest based crews. We foster opportunities within STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math) education across all content areas. Students' school hours are 8:00am - 2:51pm Mondays - Thursdays. Students are dismissed at 12:50pm on Fridays. Families may register students for the after school DYCD program that dismisses at 5:00 pm each day at no cost. At BSEA, we build exposure to our STEAM Dispositions into our curriculum in every classroom. Students learn to be problem solvers, critical thinkers, risk takers, collaborative and communicative, reflective, and focus not only on learning outcomes, but the process of the learning itself. We seek opportunities for students to exercise these dispositions through partnerships such as our NYC Junior Ambassadors program, where students attend events to develop solutions to climate change issues with Ambassadors from the United Nations or Debate, where we’ve won the Borough Championship two years in a row. At BSEA, you will be exposed to coding, robotics, engineering, design, and the arts. Our school has a STEM lab as well as individual laptops in all classrooms. We offer a wide array of sports. Students participate in flag football, soccer, track, basketball, wiffle ball, and volleyball. BSEA students attend many trips in order to bring their learning to life.

overview: Central Park East II (CPE II) is a collaborative community where staff, parents, and students work together to create a safe, caring, academically rigorous, and joyful school environment. CPE II provides an enriched education to all students that includes the arts, both visual and performing, and sports, including basketball and soccer. We have a state of the art library, a dance studio and a two-level hydroponics garden. Just a few steps from the footbridge, we use Randall's Island as an outdoor classroom. As a Community School in partnership with Children's Aid, we are able to provide many extra programs and services, including a full after-school and summer program. We participate in a variety of programs such as Urban Advantage and Civics for All. We give students the critical thinking skills, understandings, and habits of mind that will help them become thoughtful readers, writers, mathematicians, scientists, and keen observers of the world, as well as ethical agents for change. We want our students to know that their voice is important and they can use it to advocate for themselves and others to make a difference in the world.

overview: City College Magnet School of the Arts (CCMSA) is a 6-12 early college public school located in the Inwood neighborhood of northern Manhattan. In partnership with the City University of New York's (CUNY) Early College Initiative (ECI) and the City College of New York (CCNY), CCMSA provides students with an accelerated pathway to college and career readiness. Beginning as early as their freshman year, students can take free college courses at the CCNY campus, earning college credits while meeting high school graduation requirements and jumpstarting their higher education at no cost. Guided by an arts-infused, project-based curriculum, CCMSA emphasizes cognitive and skill-based learning through principles like design, problem-solving, and critique. Students can explore a variety of electives, from visual and performing arts to STEM and financial literacy, ensuring a well-rounded education. Our graduates leave as college-ready, creative, and critical thinkers, prepared to excel in their future education and careers and poised to make meaningful contributions to their communities.

overview: Being a part of the College Point Collaborative community means being part of a caring, hardworking, and supportive school family. At our school, everyone is encouraged to do their best, be kind to others, and never stop learning. Our mission is to provide an inclusive and supportive learning environment where rigorous, standards-aligned instruction and teamwork help us reach academic excellence. We are dedicated to helping every student growboth in the classroom and as a person. Our staff works together in teams to support students through the academic challenges of middle school. Our vision is to see our students become active, responsible, and productive members of the community with strong values and a love for learning that lasts a lifetime. What makes us stand out is how much we care not just about grades, but about who you are and who you can become.

overview: Community Action School is a small middle school built on the belief that every student deserves to be known, supported, and challenged. Guided by our core values of Caring, Courage, Community, and Action, our dedicated staff works collaboratively to ensure that all students receive individualized academic, social, and emotional support while engaging in rigorous and meaningful learning experiences. We place a strong emphasis on interdisciplinary learning, encouraging students to make connections across subjects and explore real-world issues from multiple perspectives. Students take advantage of New York City's rich cultural and educational resources through frequent field trips and experiences. Signature programs include our three-day camping trip to the Clearpool Environmental Education Center and our annual schoolwide Broadway trip. All 8th-grade students are enrolled in Regents-level Algebra I and Living Environment courses, providing opportunities to earn high school credit before entering 9th grade. Our advisory program focuses on goal setting, relationship building, and social-emotional development. Students also have access to a robust after-school program offering sports, arts, leadership opportunities, and academic support, as well as Saturday Academy from October through May. We encourage prospective families to learn more about our school by visiting our website, reading our reviews on InsideSchools, and scheduling a tour. Interested families may contact Principal Andrew Sullivan at asulliv@schools.nyc.gov. Diversity in Admissions (DIA): Priority to applicants eligible for free or reduced price lunch for 25% of seats.

overview:
Community Math & Science Prep is a vibrant middle school where every student is known, challenged, and celebrated. We believe that learning thrives in small groups, where teachers can tailor instruction to meet each student’s unique needs and strengths. This personalized approach supports academic growth while nurturing confidence and curiosity.
Our school is more than a place to learn it’s a place to belong. Classrooms buzz with inquiry and creativity, as students collaborate, think critically, and take intellectual risks. Beyond the classroom, students engage in experiences that build character, foster teamwork, and strengthen community.
Each spring, our students take the stage in a full Broadway Jr. production, a schoolwide event that showcases their talent, dedication, and collaboration. This is just one example of how we create meaningful opportunities for students to grow as individuals and as members of a larger community.
What sets us apart is our commitment to what works: strong relationships, thoughtful instruction, and a belief that middle school should be both rigorous and joyful. We partner closely with families and the local community to ensure that every student is supported socially, emotionally, and academically.
At Community Math & Science Prep, we don’t just prepare students for the next grade we prepare them to lead, to collaborate, and to thrive.

overview:
Here at Cornerstone Academy Middle School, we desire to cultivate a school that fosters a positive environment through open communication, collaboration, empathy, respect and celebration. We believe that students learn best in a community where they feel known, supported, and empowered. Our approach combines strong academics with a focus on student voice, social responsibility, and real-world learning. Students are encouraged to speak up, share ideas, and take active roles in their learning and community.
Small group advisory structures ensure every student is known well by at least one adult in the building. Families are active participants in the school community, with consistent communication and opportunities for engagement. We celebrate students with special incentive trips to Broadway shows, American Dream Mall, Camelback Resort, and so much more.
As a small, nurturing school, we know every child and family by name. Our principal greets students at the door each and every day. Our robust after-school program, in partnership with NYEdge, offers flag football, soccer, and basketball. We are also home to an elite dance team that competes at regional competitions. Our active PTA hosts multiple family events throughout the year, keeping our community connected and engaged. We have a brand-new computer lab and a state-of-the-art Steam LAB. Learn more at cornerstoneacademyms.org and follow us on Instagram @casabxmiddleschool

overview:
Our instructional philosophy is built on the belief that literacy is the lifeblood of education. We also believe in educating the whole child by taking learning beyond the walls of the classroom.
We offer a wide range of unique programs and opportunities in Arts Elective Program: Students can choose from a variety of arts and science courses to prepare for specialized high schools. STEM Program: Our program teaches students to tackle real-world challenges like scientists and engineers. Project-Based Learning: Our initiatives, including "CASA Community Wednesdays," allow students to engage in areas they are passionate about, such as Social Justice, STEM, Financial Literacy, and Sustainability. Dual Language Program: Families can opt their children into our Dual Language program. Accelerated Program: At the end of 6th grade, families can choose an accelerated program for 7th and 8th grade. Extracurriculars: Students can join our award-winning school band and debate team, participate in sports like basketball, volleyball, and our championship futsal team, or be active in student government.
As a PROSE (Progressive Redesign Opportunity Schools for Excellence) program school, CASA has the flexibility to innovate in teaching methods and school design. We prioritize admissions for students from low-income households, those in temporary housing, and English Language Learners to ensure a diverse and inclusive learning environment. Join us at CASA, where we empower students to reach their fullest potential.

All students at ESMS take courses in anti-bullying, resilience, healthy relationships, social and emotional literacy, and sexual health. Our after-school program offers programs in all team sports, the arts, including theater, STEAM programs, debate and Model UN. We have a vibrant LGBTQ community, and a great GSA. Our student council has worked on anti-hunger projects, no-naming calling weeks, international night and helped draft legislation that was signed into law in New York City. In our electives program, last period on Fridays, we offer classes in the arts, athletics and academics. Often, these classes are designed by and taught by our students. If a student wants to contribute to our community, it will happen. This school will give priority to applicants eligible for Free and Reduced Lunch (FRL) for up to 20 percent of seats

overview: Ebbets Field Middle School is a small, community-centered school located on the historic Jackie Robinson Campus in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. Inspired by Jackie Robinson’s legacy of perseverance, leadership, and excellence, we provide students with personalized support and opportunities that connect learning to the real world. Students can explore their interests through our Culinary Arts Program, where they develop cooking, nutrition, and entrepreneurship skills, and our Hydroponics Program, where they learn sustainable agriculture and environmental science through hands-on growing experiences. Our commitment to health and wellness is reflected in our participation in the NYC Road Runners Program, as well as our volleyball and baseball teams that promote teamwork, discipline, and school pride. Students broaden their horizons through monthly high school and college tours that expose them to future academic and career opportunities. Through partnerships with Interborough Hospital, BRIC Arts Media, and New York University, students engage in authentic learning experiences, creative arts programming, mentorship opportunities, and career exploration. Families are active partners in our school community and participate in monthly parent trips that strengthen connections between home and school. At Ebbets Field Middle School, students are challenged to become strong readers, writers, mathematicians, leaders, and problem-solvers while discovering their talents in a supportive environment where every child is known, valued, and prepared for success in high school, college, and beyond.

overview: Emolior Academy is a grade 6 to 8 college preparatory Middle School dedicated to scholars who seek an atmosphere focused on Math, Science, Technology, Engineering and the Arts. Our focus on rigorous instruction prepare our scholars to be ready for High School and experiences well beyond into their college years. We honor each student's individual mode of learning and believe that early adolescents perform best in a child-centered environment that builds self-esteem through accomplishments, and encourages individuals to explore new ideas while developing their skills, interests, and abilities. Our dedicated staff of middle school specialists has created an exciting, differentiated, interdisciplinary curriculum, which goes far beyond the New York City and State curricula, and provides for both independent and collaborative group work. Problem-solving and higher-level thinking skills are its cornerstones. We believe in a home-school partnership and encourage our parents to take an active role in their child's academic experiences. All Scholars are empowered to prepare for the specialized high school entrance exams starting from the 6th grade and also take a minimum of one out of four regents level courses offered in the 8th grade.

overview: E.S.M.T. - I.S. 190 is located at 1550 Crotona Park East, Bronx, NY 10460. We share the building with Francisco Oller Community School 61 (C.S. 61). We are a collaborative school community dedicated to improving our students' academic performance while fostering their physical, mental, social, and emotional growth. We provide a nurturing environment, standards and data driven instruction to address the needs of each student. Through continued collaboration of parents, administrators, staff, and community-based organizations, we will prepare every student to meet the needs of an ever-changing society. We envision that each student values education, holds high personal and educational expectations, is accountable for his/her own learning, communicates effectively, excels in all areas, connects school and real-life situations, and develops into a life-long learner. We offer the following academic subjects: English Language Arts, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, Physical/Health Education, Visual Arts, Music, and AIS. As part of College and Career Readiness, three Regents courses are offered in Grade 8: Algebra 1, U.S. History and Government, and Biology. We enrich and supplement our school curriculum through academic and non-academic activities such as After School Academy, educational trips to colleges/universities, Broadway shows, parks, museums, and other educational institutions. We are in partnership with East Side House. It is a Community Based Organization that supports family and community engagement in our school. It offers after school and summer programs in different areas - academic, sports, arts, technology, and leadership skills. It prepares our students to face academic and social challenges in middle school and beyond.

overview: Esperanza Preparatory Magnet School's middle school program (Grades 6-8) lays the foundation for academic excellence by preparing students for the rigor of high school, college, and future careers. Guided by our Magnet themes of Early College, Exploration, and Leadership, students engage in a challenging curriculum that emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and technology integration. Through personalized instruction, leadership opportunities, project-based learning, and enrichment programs, students develop the skills and confidence needed to succeed academically and personally. Beginning in middle school, students have the opportunity to accelerate their learning by taking high school-level coursework, earning high school credits, and sitting for New York State Regents examinations before entering ninth grade. This early exposure allows students to build a strong academic transcript, explore advanced learning opportunities, and position themselves for Advanced Placement (AP), College Now, and other Early College experiences in high school. By starting this pathway in the middle grades, Esperanza ensures students are well-prepared to maximize their high school experience, graduate with college credits, and confidently pursue college, careers, and leadership opportunities.

overview:
On behalf of the Evergreen Middle School for Urban Exploration community, thank you for your interest in our school. We are a vibrant community committed to nurturing independent and creative thinkers, self-advocates, urban explorers, inventors, and leaders through authentic learning experiences. We work collaboratively with families to foster the academic, social, emotional, and cognitive growth of our students. We proudly celebrate the diversity of perspectives, experiences, and talents in our community.
Students have the opportunity to benefit from several key programs:
The Middle School Quality Initiative (MSQI): This initiative supports school-wide literacy practices across all subjects.
Edible Schoolyard: Through a farm-to-table model, our students learn how to grow and cook sustainable, organic food in our garden and kitchen classrooms.
Showcase School: We are proud to have been a Showcase Schools host for the 2018-2019 school year.
Teacher Recruitment Partnership: Our teachers and students help prepare student teachers to enter the classroom.
To ensure all students are college and career ready, we offer: One-to-one laptops, Computer Science for All, Civics for All, College Access for All, and Regents courses in Algebra and Living Environment.
We are proud to have concluded the 2020-21 school year with a 95% student attendance rate, the highest in District 32.

overview:
The Facing History Middle School is a small, inclusive learning community serving students in grades 6 through 12. Known for its warm, family-like atmosphere, the school emphasizes meaningful relationships and a supportive environment where every student is seen and valued.
Facing History embraces a project-based learning model, engaging students in hands-on, real-world projects that foster critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration. The school is also rooted in restorative justice practices, promoting a culture of accountability, empathy, and community building over traditional disciplinary approaches.
Rather than using traditional letter grades, the school implements a competency-based grading system, allowing students to demonstrate mastery of key skills and concepts at their own pace. This approach supports deeper learning and personal growth, helping students understand both what they are learning and why it matters.
With its unique blend of rigorous academics, social-emotional learning, and community-centered values, The Facing History Middle School prepares students not just for high school and college, but for thoughtful, engaged citizenship in a diverse and changing world.

overview: Fannie Lou Hamer Middle School is a small school where students develop skills to work effectively, think critically, and act compassionately so that they can advocate for themselves and their communities as they go out into the world. We will offer a new Dual Language English/Spanish program for incoming 6th graders that we are very excited about for Fall 2024. At FLHMS, we believe that work in school should not only help students master the standards for each grade, but should also be relevant to their lives and represent authentic opportunities to use their knowledge and skills to make a difference in the community. Each student builds a portfolio over their three years at FLHMS, presenting selected pieces from the portfolio and Roundtables twice a year in each grade for feedback from other students, teachers, and family and community members. Students gain important speaking and presentation skills during Roundtables and have the opportunity to see how their work in middle school is applicable to the work they will do in high school, college, and their future careers. Before leaving FLHMS, each student has the opportunity to engage in a wide range of opportunities from participating performance and visual art productions, being a member of a sports and academic teams, and taking college and overnight trips out of the city.

overview: At Fort Greene Prep, we believe that middle school is a time for scholars to explore their interests and begin to learn about who they are. Our inquiry-based curriculum is designed to provide a wide array of content and extra-curricular experiences that allow scholars to engage in our learning pathways, and in grade 8, focus on a pathway of their choice. Our pathways include Visual Arts programming in drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, digital art, and ceramics and enriched through partnerships with Studios in a School, Strike Anywhere, and Irondale Theater support this work. New this year is the addition of a music pathway. STEM is engaged through hands-on experimentation in the classroom, interactive field work in partnership with Urban Advantage Science, and engaging enrichment in partnership with the organizations Citizen Science and Code.org. Our World Language pathway allows opportunities to study either Spanish or French and offers a continuing pathway in French Dual Language (FDL) for children who are graduating from an elementary FDL program. We are proud of our inclusive programming that supports our children within an Integrated Co-teaching model and flexible programming to support our Students with Disabilities and Multi-lingual Learners. We provide enriching afterschool programming and opportunities for advanced studies in preparation for high school including opportunities to take the Algebra and Living Environment Regents, and the World Language Proficiency. Our FDL students are prepared to be on track for the Seal of Biliteracy as they enter high school. Our scholars develop social-emotional capacity through our Advisory Program, putting students at the center of their learning and empowering our children to build an equitable culture together.

overview: Global Innovators Academy (MS 428), located in Sunset Park, is a dual-language middle school in District 15. As a trailblazing school grounded in project-based learning, we are committed to cultivating the next generation of compassionate global citizens who are bilingual, biliterate, and bicultural. Our mission is to harness the power of language, rigorous academics, and cross-cultural collaboration to prepare students for an ever-evolving world. We strive to foster a safe and inclusive learning environment that values each individual’s strengths, identity, culture, and heritage, while building a harmonious and diverse community. At MS 428, we prioritize high academic achievement through an equitable, culturally responsive curriculum enriched with integrated project-based learning. Students engage in meaningful opportunities to collaborate with diverse populations through workshops and community-centered projects that promote real-world impact. A hallmark of our school model is our innovative approach to language learning. We provide interdisciplinary instruction by embedding community service and project-based experiences into the core curriculum, empowering students to apply their language skills in authentic and meaningful ways. Through thoughtful scheduling and a high-quality, inclusive curriculum, we ensure that all learners-regardless of background have equitable access to opportunities that prepare them for college, career, and beyond. Opening in September 2024, Global Innovators Academy welcomes students who are inspired by an immersive dual-language experience and eager to grow as leaders. Our students actively participate in community-building initiatives that cultivate leadership, global awareness, and the skills needed to thrive in the world of tomorrow.

overview: At Hamilton Grange success looks different for each of us. For some, it is starring in our 55-piece band, our school musical, or painting on one of our famous murals. For others it is participating in a combination of activities that include competing as members of one of our 15 athletic teams (cheerleading, soccer, basketball, baseball, softball, boxing, bouldering, football, fencing, sailing, and hiking). We pride ourselves on providing myriad opportunities to our students through school day electives like theater, visual arts, music, dance, and weightlifting, and supporting academic success through culturally responsive teaching practices. All of our students select an arts major in grades 7 and 8 and receive daily instruction in their chosen artform. We have earned local and national recognition for our students' academic growth and our progressive approach to discipline - we use restorative practices rather than detentions or suspensions (We have twice been named a NYC Showcase School for School Culture, were NY State's only middle grades Reward School in 2017-18 because our kids made more progress on their state exams than any other students at any other school in NY State, and Teach for America named us 1 of just 4 Schools To Learn From in the United States in 2018-2019). The overwhelming majority of our students are accepted to the City's most selective high schools through their scores on the SHSAT and via auditions in the arts. We also offer high school credit through accelerated, Regents courses in Algebra, Biology, and US History. We hope to see you soon!

overview: Hawtree Creek Middle School (HCMS), opened in September 2013, is a small middle school co-located within the Virgil I. Grissom Campus in South Ozone Park. HCMS serves a diverse population of approximately 375 students.The mission and vision of the school is dedicated to developing students as leaders prepared to enter high school with a set of skills and a body of knowledge that will serve each student beyond high school. The school boasts a strong college-going culture and each student visits 3-5 college campuses before he/she graduates. Some features that support our college-going culture include development of the school character traits: Community, Perseverance, Collaboration, and Leadership; student-led conferences twice a year; the school-wideindependent reading program; collaborative study groups and student to student dialogue in each class; being an AVID Showcase School; and being a pilot school for College Access For All in 2014.Academic values include developing communication, research, and problem-solving skills in each of our students.Instruction is differentiated, giving all students the direction and support needed to master these skills and engage in rigorous content on a daily basis.

overview: HPCS is a collaborative school in which students, parents, and teachers work together to improve the learning outcomes and opportunities available to students. At HPCS, we pride ourselves on ensuring that students are active participants in their educational journey. As a school, we expose students to rigorous instruction and various stem opportunities that wouldprepare them to become empowered leaders that will thrive in the 21st Century. Students are offered the opportunity to participate in advance regents courses. We ensure equity for all by attending to the individualized student needs so that all students will achieve academic success. Students receive instruction that is culturally relevant, rigorous, and includes opportunities to problem solve, collaborate with their peers, and clearly communicate their thinking. We are aVILS School which means that students have access to technology to advance their learning and teachers are provided with training on technological supports that can be used to increase student engagement and enhance learning experiences. Students benefit from this program because it provides them with easy access to information, it accelerates their learning, attend to their varied learning styles, and provide fun ways for students to practice what they are learning. The over-arching goal of HPCS is to empower students to be leaders and bold thinkers that are prepared to be successful in the careers of the future. We work to restore the love for school, having kids enjoy learning, feel supported, and advocate for activities of their interests.

overview: Irwin Altman Middle School 172 is located in a "suburban" setting in Floral Park, Queens. The school's dedicated, experienced and caring staff use a student-centered middle school philosophy that supports our goal of all students achieving academic excellence in a safe and supportive environment. We honor and celebrate the diversity of our MS 172 community. Our curriculum emphasizes academic exploration and collaborative experiences in the development of critical thinking. Approximately 1/2 of our grade 8 students earn HS credit in science, math, social studies and foreign language. MS 172 is in ongoing partnership with the UA Science Initiative highlighting collaborations with science cultural institutions, with Reel Works to provide students with curriculum-related moving image and filming experiences, with SAYA! (South Asian Youth Action,) in offering a Girls' Leadership Group, with the Ronald McDonald House for community service opportunities, and with the DOE C.H.A.M.P.S. program to provide before and after-school sports. In partnership with the Common Point Queens Beacon, we can provide additional after school and holiday activities. Students at MS 172 have participated in and have received honors in the Games for Change Challenge, the NYS School Music Association competition, and several art and debate competitions.

overview: Horace Greeley I.S. 10 stands out as a vibrant, inclusive middle school rooted in the diverse and growing community of Long Island City, Queens. With students from a wide range of cultural backgrounds, our school provides a welcoming environment that values individual differences and promotes mutual respect. We offer a wide range of academic programs to meet the needs of all learners, including self-contained special education, ICT, ELL, and accelerated classes. Technology is integrated throughout the building, with wireless access, laptops, and digital tools available in every classroom to support modern, engaging instruction. What truly sets us apart are the real-world learning opportunities we offerfrom staging full-scale drama productions and showcasing student art to participating in hands-on science through Urban Advantage or practicing Italian at a local restaurant. Our students can also join clubs in chess, hydroponics, photography, and e-sports, gaining experiences that go beyond the traditional classroom. These opportunities reflect our school s vision: to nurture confident, capable learners through strong instruction, cultural enrichment, and community partnership, preparing every student for success now and in the future.

overview: I.S. 27, Anning S. Prall Intermediate School is a New York City Public School serving grades 6 through 8. We proudly serve the West Brighton community in Staten Island. We strive for our students to be the center of a joyful, rigorous, culturally relevant, and a highly effective learning environment. Our greatest strength is our diversity, and I.S. 27 students collaboratively develop the necessary academic, social, and emotional skills to positively impact themselves, their family, and the community. We strive to embed STREAM (science, technology, reading/robotics, engineering, arts, and math) into all learning experiences, preparing us to become 21st century leaders. As we listen deeply, we hope to empower students' voice and choice in their education. Our goal is to know our students well so we can meet their learning and social needs.

overview: At Edwin Markham Intermediate School 51, students have the opportunity to choose from three enrichment academies that allow them to explore their interests while developing new skills.Our academy options include Performing Arts (Band, Dance, and Drama), Fine Arts (Art, Digital Art, Virtual Enterprise and Music Production), and Video Robotics. Students participate in their selected enrichment program daily, providing meaningful opportunities for creativity, collaboration, and hands-on learning.Our rigorous academic program prepares students for success in high school, college, and future careers. We provide targeted support and accelerated learning opportunities for all students, including opportunities to earn high school credit through Regents-level courses in Biology, Algebra I, and U.S. History, as well as Spanish Proficiency. In addition to our academy programs, I.S. 51 offers a comprehensive after-school program featuring a wide variety of clubs and activities designed to meet the diverse interests of our students. Athletic opportunities include Basketball, Baseball, Bowling, Track, Softball, Volleyball, and Soccer, promoting teamwork, sportsmanship, and healthy lifestyles.

overview: Adolescence is a unique, exciting and challenging time of life. Students at this age are experiencing profound changes - physically, emotionally, socially and intellectually - as they pass through a very special and critical period of their lives. Realizing that the success of students in middle level grades is often the forerunner of success in high school, college and beyond, Morris Intermediate School is committed to ensuring the transition to adolescence is a positive experience by providing students with a caring and supportive school community.In addition, our primary focus is to engage our students in a rigorous and comprehensive curriculum that promotes critical thinking and problem solving, while providing equity for all students.Our mission is to prepare all students for the world beyond Morris by providing a solid academic foundation, as we seek to promote positive self-worth and a sense of responsibility for themselves and others.

overview: At Frank D. Paulo Intermediate School, teachers foster a life-long passion for learning in their students. We strive to educate the whole child focusing on all facets of student growth, including social emotional learning, problem solving and the highest level of subject mastery. Students will be prepared for the 21st century world, becoming productive, contributing and responsible citizens. Digital tools are integrated into the instruction throughout the day as students have access to Chomebooks or iPads in all of their classrooms. The essence of our efforts here at Paulo is to assure that each student realizes his or her unique potential of body, mind, and spirit that he or she may possess, and graduates from I.S. 75 prepared both academically and socially to pursue rewarding college and career paths in this challenging 21st century world . In addition to our traditional program, we offer both Nest and ACES programs for students who benefit from additional support. Our efforts are supported by our extensive after school program comprised of cultural, technological, sports, social, and academic clubs, to which all students have access.

overview: The motto of IS 77, 'A Family of Learners,' illustrates the commitment of the faculty and staff. Our parent coordinator, Ms. Carmen Resto, holds monthly lunch and learn workshops for parents in English, as well as in Spanish. Some topics include Cyber-bulling, Understanding the Common Core Learning Standards, School Safety, and other topics addressing the academic, emotional and social well-being of our students. IS 77 recognizes that in order to meet the diverse needs of the students and families of this community, we offer a variety of programs and activities in addition to our core academic subjects. In addition, our school has maintained an ongoing relationship with feeder schools. The IS 77 Holiday concert features a combined chorus of our students as well as the feeder schools! Our Chourus is invited to particpate in a local HS holiday concert! IS 77 is the recipient of a NYS Expanded Learning Time grant. The intent of this program is to provide IS 77 students the opportunity to participate in an extended school day, week and year in order to better meet the needs of its students and school community and improve student achievement. Among our programs is our award winning STEM program featuring our robotics club! Now offering a STEM Program where students learn to think and act as scientists and engineers, identify and explore real-world challenges, while building computational thinking, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.

Students participate in cheerleading, basketball, volleyball, badminton, archery, and soccer. Students are involved in National Junior Honor Society and community service projects. Some students participate in our 3-year Spanish Dual Language Honors Program. They can also be a part of our Student Government and School Leadership Team. Some students join rock band and drum line.Students are involved in our Annual Science Expo, Annual Arts Extravaganza, two drama productions, the Annual Beacon Show, and our Annual Talent Show. 8th graders have the chance to earn H.S. Regents credit in Algebra, Biology, and Earth & Space. Students in our SHSAT program are prepared for specialized high schools. We also offer successful reading interventions tailored to the needs of our students.We survey our students to identify their top interests and match them to real activities and events.This list of learning opportunities continues to grow.

overview: The Wade Academies MS 117X is a Community School that serves as a beacon for our neighborhood. Through a strong partnership with The Community Association for Progressive Dominicans (ACDP), we offer extensive support to our students and their families. We provide a wide range of services, including: Academic & Mentorship Support: college trips, on-site mentors, and opportunities for students to earn high school Regents credits. Family & Community Services: monthly food pantry access, parent classes, health and wellness workshops, free vision screenings and glasses, on-site dental and immigration services, and access to a washer and dryer. Mental Health Support: We offer mental health services and referrals to support our community. We have a diverse student body, with a large population of English Language Learners and students with disabilities. We offer a Traditional Bilingual Education Program (TBE), a Special Education Bilingual Program, and a freestanding English as a Second Language Program (FSESL) for students in grades 6-8. Our teachers use data-informed practices to design learning experiences that help all students reach mastery in literacy and mathematics. Our vision, guided by our core values of civic leadership, community, justice, and learning, is to foster an inclusive environment that prepares all students to become curious, socially just, and high-achieving citizens. We believe in an open-door policy for families and engage them through workshops, student performances, and school activities.

Our mission is to develop programs to include performing arts, accelerated courses, foreign languages and STEAM, while giving our learners the opportunity to feel empowered through their voice, ability to make choice and support in decision making.

overview: IS 125Q is a vibrant learning community that reflects the greater Queens borough. We use Restorative Practices to promote positive behaviors, address conflict, and provide a supportive and inclusive education. Our Arts Department offers students 8 different tracks: Band, Chorus, Dance, Digital Arts (3D Printing), Drama, Music Theory, Orchestra, and Visual Arts. We offer students competitive athletics in basketball, soccer, and track, as well as intramural sports like volleyball, badminton, cheer, and weight training. Our Regents program offers qualifying students the opportunity to earn high school credit for 4 Regents exams: Algebra, English, U.S. History and Government, and Earth Science or Living Environment. We offer a variety of clubs and activities, including Minecraft, LEGO Robotics, our school newspaper, and Anime club. Our STEM program is linked with NY Sunworks, and we offer tutoring and Regents prep throughout the school year. Instagram: @IS125Q

overview:
AtMiddle School 136, we provide students with access to a rigorous and engaging curriculum aligned to the New York State Next Generation Learning Standards. Our instructional program is designed to build on students’ strengths, lived experiences, cultures, and interests while ensuring all students have access to grade-level content and opportunities for academic success.
Students have the opportunity to become bilingual and biliterate through our Spanish Dual Language Program or study French as a World Language. Our school also prioritizes the development of the whole child by embedding social-emotional learning, restorative practices, advisory, and Dewey’s 4 C’s - Curiosity, Collaboration, Commitment, and Courage -into daily instruction and school culture.
Beyond the classroom, students can explore their interests and talents through a variety of extracurricular activities, leadership opportunities, sports teams, and student clubs. Students may participate in programs such as visual arts, theater, dance, vocal and instrumental music, debate, student government, NJHS, athletics, and other enrichment experiences that foster confidence, leadership, and personal growth.
At Dewey, we are committed to creating a safe, inclusive, and supportive learning environment where every student feels valued, challenged, and empowered. We believe in educating the whole child and preparing students to thrive in high school, college, careers, and beyond.
Diversity in Admissions (DIA): Priority is given to applicants eligible for free or reduced-price lunch, students in temporary housing, and English Language Learners for 52% of available seats.

overview: Nestled in the heart of multicultural Astoria, I.S. 141 The Steinway School has ranked among the top 20% of schools for the past decade. We provide rigorous, inquiry-based instruction in a caring, supportive, and highly engaging environment where students are empowered to learn through collaborative exploration and critical thinking. At I.S. 141, we believe students learn best when actively engaged in meaningful, hands-on learning experiences that foster curiosity, creativity, and ownership, and our mission is to ensure that every student thrives in collaborative, culturally responsive classrooms where academic excellence, equity, and social-emotional well-being are prioritized. Working together with administrators, teachers, families, and students, we cultivate a school community in which every stakeholder feels like apirate on a daring and adventurous educational journey. We are proud to offer an Accelerated Program that provides in-depth study and prepares students for Regents examinations in Biology, U.S. History and Government, and Algebra I, while also promoting the arts and humanities through music, visual arts, and computer arts programs that encourage creativity, innovation, and self-expression. As part of our commitment to preparing students for success in college, careers, and civic life, I.S. 141 proudly participates in New York City Public Schools initiatives, including College Access for All, Algebra for All, Civics for All, Computer Science for All, and the SHSAT Program, ensuring students develop the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to become lifelong learners and leaders in an ever-changing world.

overview: Middle School 181 is focused on developing the whole child through a balance of academic and enrichment opportunities in the arts (see activities). M.S. 181 offers two outstanding programs. Our Community Service program is deeply embedded in rigorous curriculum and the fundamental ideologies of 21st Century Learning. Engaging activities in which investigating, problem solving and students at the center of learning. All students are provided with their own device and participate in a two-year, four course STEM program, in which they cycle through two unique courses each year. These courses journey students through hands-on, project-based learning experiences using technology. Students apply computer coding skills to program flying drones, build objects using 3D printing, and create working robots. All students participate in a special 3-year Mathematics that culminates with all grade 8 students being offered the opportunity to participate in the Algebra 1 Regents exam. Students in the honors program participate in the 11th grade U.S. History course and 9th grade Biology courseThese accelerated courses culminate with taking Regents exams and earning high school credit in their eighth grade year. Honors students also participate in the STEM experiences listed above. M.S. 181 believes that it is essential for our students to give back and therefore all children at our school are involved in supporting our community and making a difference in the lives of others. Students develop and lead an array of community service projects within the school, such as Toy Drives, Autism Awareness activities, fundraising for cancer research, and kindness campaigns. A dress code is in place at M.S. 181. Each grade level is assigned a specific polo shirt color to wear.

overview: At Renaissance Middle School we are committed to preparing students for college and careers. We strive to inspire and empower students to excel both academically and socially, while preparing them to be productive citizens and future leaders. To that end, RMS aims to provide a nurturing and safe environment that fosters a rigorous academic curriculum to prepare students to become lifelong learners. To ensure students are prepared to be future leaders we offer a variety of accelerated courses including Algebra I, Biology, English And US Government. We also offer student selected Talent courses such as Music, Dance and Visual Arts to encourage creativity. In addition to all of that, we encourage leadership through extracurricular activities such as Student Government, Peer Mediation, Soil Society garden club, Step, Volleyball, Soccer, Nursing Club and so much more. Our students have the opportunity to join after-school programs through our partnerships with Boys & Girls Club of Queens Metro and Queensborough Community College. We are fully committed to cultivating an academic environment that will ensure whole-child success. We look forward to welcoming you to the RMS family!

overview: I.S. 206B is a middle school where all students are inspired to be life-long learners in the 21st century and feel safe taking academic risks, delving deeper into learning, collaborating, and being responsible and productive citizens. At I.S. 206B, students are engaged in rich and meaningful learning experiences, such as coding, drone building, dancing, visual arts, Regents courses, debate, volleyball, football, soccer, basketball, chess, dance, and many more. In the supportive learning environment, students are encouraged to challenge, question, and think critically to solve real-world problems while interacting with rigorous curriculum. All students have access to before, during, and after school academic supports. Students at I.S. 206B are trained in leadership skills through the LeaderInMe and BrainPower programs. Students gain extended learning experiences through the partnership with The Good Shepherd's program, a community-based organization. As a member of the Middle School Quality Initiative (MSQI), all students gain key literacy instruction to build skills necessary for success in high school and college and 21st century careers.

overview: At John Wilson Intermediate School 211, we are fearless in the pursuit of excellence. Rooted in the core values of Tenacity, Integrity, Growth, Excellence, Responsibility, and Strength, we cultivate a supportive and inclusive learning environment where every student is empowered to thrive. Our school is committed to academic rigor and innovation, offering accelerated Algebra courses and integrating technology across all classrooms to enhance learning. Students benefit from unique opportunities such as our state-of-the-art hydroponics lab, which fosters hands-on exploration and environmental awareness. John Wilson I.S. 211 proudly supports diverse learners through honors classes, self-contained classrooms, integrated co-teaching classes, and the only ACES program in District 18. We prepare students for high school and beyond by offering challenging coursework and early exposure to college and career pathways. Our students participate annually in the Science Fair, Spelling Bee, and Debate League showcasing their talents and academic growth. We celebrate student success through Honor Roll recognition and other academic achievements throughout the year. Our vibrant after-school program, running daily until 5:15 PM, offers a wide range of extracurricular activities including basketball, soccer, dance, cheerleading, chess, SHSAT prep, and various clubs that promote creativity, leadership, and teamwork. We believe in learning beyond the classroom, offering enriching field trips and monthly family engagement events that strengthen our school community. At I.S. 211, we don't just educate, we inspire. We are the pride and joy of Canarsie, committed to excellence for ourselves and a stronger, more connected community.

overview: The Louis Armstrong Middle School is a borough wide school that offers free stop to stop busing for all students in Queens. We opened in 1979 by a court order to ensure diversity with the mission of bringing together a group of culturally diverse children to help them grow academically, socially, emotionally, and physically. As required by the court order, the racial identification and home address of applicants will be considered in admissions as well as equity in academic standing. At LAMS students are provided a personalized caring and supportive environment. The staff works to build the principals of STRIVE.Whereas, S stands for Self-Regulation, T- Tenacity, R-Respect, I-Integrity, V- Vision, E-Empathy. At LAMS we believe in a strong standards-based rigorous curriculum to help guide and accelerate our students. We also believe in using standards-based assessments to drive our instruction. In addition to the core subjects, LAMS offers accelerated Regents courses in Algebra, Geometry, Living Environment, Earth Science, and US History. Our English Language Learners program offers full immersion and supports to ensure rigorous instruction while our MLL students work toward language mastery. The school is affiliated with Queens College, Vaughn College, National Middle School Association and National Reform Policy. Our school is an original recipient of the US President Award for Excellence, and has been consistently a Rewards/Recognition status school, and by the NASSP as being one of the top, most effective middle schools in the United States.

overview: The Dr. Roland Patterson School (09x229) is located next to the Roberto Clemente State Park, on the banks of the Harlem River. With a student : teacher ratio of less than 1 : 10, our school takes pride in knowing and caring for the social and emotional needs of every student.This is the hallmark of 229 -- that every student has an adult in the school building who is their champion, who looks out for their emotional and academic well-being every single day.Our new Response to Intervention Program guarantees that every day students get what they need in order to advance academically. We are proud to provide classes to students who are in the autistic spectrum. With two classes serving sixteen students, the Horizons program meets the special needs of this community. Our intensive approach to education features many classes where two adults are present to support instruction and supervise small-group work. 229 just invested in serious educational technology: every classroom has a new SmartBoard and a document projector. Every student is assigned a laptop, and GoogleClassroom is used in many classes.

overview: Intermediate School 230Q is a zoned middle school in Jackson Heights, Queens. Our student body is diverse, and the vast majority of our students demonstrate an acceptance of individual differences. The school's organizational structure is focused upon continued improvement of instruction. Leadership and faculty implement common core aligned curricula and tasks across grades and content areas, promoting college and career readiness for all students. Starting in grade seven, all students have a choice of Vocal Music, Band or Visual Arts, and receive three periods per week. Most eighth graders take the NYS Regents in Algebra and Living Environment. Eligible eighth graders take the NYC Second Language Proficiency Exam in Spanish to receive HS credit. A wide variety of after school enrichment programs and clubs are available for all interests. Our sixth grade is housed in our Annex building, which is directly across the street from the main building. This smaller environment for grade six helps support students in the social/emotional transition to middle school.

Many students go on to attend Stuyvesant, Bronx Science, and Brooklyn Tech. English language learners receive instruction before, after, and during the school day as well as on Saturdays. All students receive instruction in visual arts, band, strings, or chorus. Our extended day programs include academic tutoring, basketball, musical theater, guitar, keyboard, and art. Our Debate and Math teams have won multiple district, borough, and city-wide tournaments. SONYC, a free after-school program, offers homework help and recreational activities Monday through Friday from 2:20pm-5pm, Monday and Wednesday evenings from 6pm-7:30pm, and operates during most school holidays. We welcome parent involvement at all times.

overview: Welcome to I.S. 285 Meyer Levin School for the Performing Arts, a vibrant middle school at 5909 Beverly Road in East Flatbush, Brooklyn (District 18). Serving grades 6-8, Meyer Levin is school that welcomes creative young minds from across all boroughs through its specialized performing arts admissions program. Our school operates on "The 5 Cs," ensuring our students grow to be Courageous, Collaborative, Creative, Competitive, and Cultured. At Meyer Levin, self-expression and academic excellence go hand in hand. Our legendary arts department allows students to specialize in intensive talent majors and perform on major stages across NYC. These specialized studios include our renowned Steel Drum Orchestra, which teaches the rich history and rhythms of steel pan music; our Musical Theater and Drama program, where students learn acting and stage design for full-scale productions; our Dance department, which explores classic and contemporary choreography; and our Instrumental and Vocal Music tracks. While creativity is our heartbeat, academic rigor is our foundation. We prepare students for competitive high schools through our accelerated "Astral" program, allowing eighth graders to take high-school-level Regents classes in Living Environment and Algebra I for early credit. We also offer STEM enrichment featuring Robotics, comprehensive English as a New Language (ENL) support, integrated Special Education services, and targeted SHSAT preparation. To foster focus and pride, Meyer Levin enforces a school uniform policy. Our campus supports families with free daily breakfast at 7:30 AM, extended-day after-school programming, and Saturday Academies. The school is accessible via the B7, B8, B17, B35, B46, and B47 buses. Explore Meyer Levin on your MySchools dashboard!

overview: AtI.S 303 we believe that all children are capable of excellence. It is our goal as a school community to have each of our students reach their maximum potential not only academically, but socially and emotionally as well. We believe that with heart, and strong character, all children can be successful citizens who make positive contributions to society. Honesty, empathy, accountability, respect, and teamwork (HEART)are the core values that we strive to build within our students inside and outside of the classroom.Our teachers work to build collaborative classroom environments where all students have the opportunity to be successful through hands-on projects that are reflective of real world situations. Students are challenged in all of their their classes, with opportunities to take advanced regents courses in mathematics and science. In addition to academic programs, we also give students the opportunity to explore various talent areas including music, dance, STEM, media, and art. Our classrooms are a safe haven for students where they are supported to reach new heights and discover new interests.With our new Russian Dual Language program, we continue to embrace the diversity of our community. Through the Russian Dual Language program, students have the chance to earn a Seal of Biliteracy in Russian and in English. Our diversity is our strength. We want all of our students to value who they are and where they come from.At I.S 303, students display Heart, give Heart,and receive Heart in all that they do. Each child is given an educational experience tailored to their needs. Through high expectations and positive teacher student relationships we ensure that all of our children have the tools to be successful in middle school, high school, and beyond.
