overview:
At I.S. 347 School of Humanities, our mission is to invest in the future of every child by giving them the tools they need to thrive as lifelong learners and productive citizens in a collaborative, inclusive, and supportive environment. Guided by our motto, Where You Belong, we create a school where every student feels seen, valued, and inspired to succeed academically, socially, and emotionally.
Our diverse Brooklyn community celebrates many cultures and languages. We proudly support multilingual learners, students with disabilities, and families from all backgrounds. Our dedicated teachers provide rigorous, equitable instruction while empowering students to set goals, reflect, and grow with confidence.
We nurture a joyful, positive school culture through our You Belong initiative, student leadership opportunities, restorative practices, and our PBIS values: Radiant, Respect, and Relentless. Here, students build strong relationships, develop leadership skills, and truly feel at home.
Students can discover their passions through extensive extracurricular programs, including competitive sports teams and a vibrant film and media program. Our exciting NASA STEM partnership offers hands-on scientific learning that sparks curiosity and innovation.
Through strong partnerships with organizations like Good Shepherd Services, YMCA Beacon, Urban Advantage, and NYC CHAMPS, we provide enriching academic, social, and emotional supports beyond the classroom.
At I.S. 347, your child will be challenged, supported, and celebrated every day.
Join our community where you belong and where your future shines. I.S. 347, Together We Shine.

overview:
I.S. 381 offers an intimate, personalized, and nurturing environment where academic rigor is valued. Our staff works collaboratively to develop enriched, individualized curricula to meet students' needs. We offer accelerated courses like Living Environment, Algebra, and American History, which lead to Regents credits.
As students move through the grades, they participate in three separate academies: 6th Grade: Academy of Dramatic and Fine Arts (ADAFA): Students engage in a program dedicated to nurturing new and existing talents through coursework, performances, and showcases. 7th Grade: Academy of Law and Civics: Students are introduced to careers in law, the courts, and law enforcement. Enrichment courses focus on legal issues, and students participate in role-playing, public speaking, and fun, law-themed trips. 8th Grade: Medical Science Academy: This program prepares students for high school by visiting science museums, colleges with STEAM majors, and local medical facilities. Students also network with current medical and science professionals.
These academies offer enrichment coursework to prepare students for prestigious high school programs.
Our school also has partnerships with several organizations, including New York Edge, Girl Be Heard, and CHAMPS, which provide our morning and after-school programs. Additionally, we offer a renowned STEAM Enrichment After-School program with offerings like Flag Football, STEM Design, Visual Arts, and Empower U/Nutrition.
I.S. 381 participates in several Chancellor's initiatives, including Algebra for All, College Access for All, Computer Science for All, and Civics for All Partner Programs.

overview: Intermediate School 392, located in Brooklyn, is a grade 6-8 middle school with over 300 students. Our mission is to establish and maintain a school environment that is challenging and nurturing. At IS 392 we equip students with the tools for success both educationally and emotionally. We promote academic excellence and digital acuity by infusing the arts and professional competencies to prepare students for college and careers. IS 392 scholars engage in high levels of academic achievement utilizing a rigorous, interdisciplinary curriculum focusing on the higher-order thinking skills of application, synthesis, and evaluation. This curriculum infuses the arts, creates articulate public speakers, and encourages students to become productive members of society. Student led classrooms are grounded in questioning, writing, discussion, and inquiry to create high-level learning experiences in all content areas.Learning tasks are developed to promote student thinking and invite students to explain their thinking. The Leadership Program provides mentoring for at-risk students with successful role models from the community. In order to build school spirit and develop students' personal interests, we offer various after-school programs. Parents are also significant contributors within the school community, working harmoniously with the staff to ensure their children's success. At I.S. 392, we truly live by the mantra of the African proverb: "It takes a whole village to raise a child."

At Dreyfus, your child will be part of a community that believes in their potential, supports their growth, and celebrates their unique journey every step of the way. We are not just preparing students for high school, we are shaping the leaders of tomorrow.

overview: At I.S. 5 We Talk Like Scholars, Write Like Experts, Think Like Innovators and Live Like Leaders! Students appreciate that I.S. 5 provides them with a welcoming, affirming and nurturing environment that pairs the development of academic strengths with the deepening of socio-emotional skills to prepare our young people to be dynamic leaders. At I.S. 5 we have four Communities, each with an assigned assistant principal and school counselor who work with students through all three years. Our I.S. 5 Scholars, Experts, Innovators and Leaders all engage in weekly advisory classes that champion our I.S. 5 Core Values: respect, integrity, empathy, accountability and, most importantly, building connection and community with each other. I.S. 5 academics include a unified and rigorous shared curriculum, paired with a range of learning opportunities to address areas of need and enrichment during our What I Need (WIN) periods. Our students have opportunities to learn about their future through career days, guest speakers, school trips, performances and exciting partnerships with high schools, colleges and professional organizations. From hands-on projects that highlight citizenship and contribution, to science investigations, to math explorations, to literacy spotlights on the lived experiences of our students, we believe at I.S. 5 that our studies stretch well beyond the classroom. Our current curriculum offers World Language Spanish, Fine and Performing Arts classes, Computer Science, Civic Leadership, and Financial Literacy. We are proud to offer The I.S. 5 Dual Language Program in Spanish and The I.S. 5 Leadership in STEM Program, each of which provide another avenue for students to join our amazing school. We hope you consider being a part of the I.S. 5 school community!

overview: Isaac Newton Middle School for Math & Science is part of a select cohort of schools offering School Based Virtual Learning. Beginning SY2526, our students will have remote learning opportunities while students unable to participate remotely can report to the building for the same experience. We foster a rigorous academic environment preparing students for high school success and cultivate a community where students broaden their intellectual horizons and develop into well-informed, engaged citizens. Our curriculum emphasizes core academic and social skills with technology integration. Students leverage technology to enhance learning and develop responsible digital citizenship. We offer diverse electives including chorus, theatre, visual arts, PE, health, technology, foreign language, and tutorials. Eighth graders tackle rigorous college preparatory curriculum with Regents-level coursework in Algebra I, Living Environment, and Global History, preparing them for high school's academic demands. Located in vibrant East Harlem near the East River, our school features modern classrooms with air conditioning, iPads, Apple TVs, and SmartBoards. Jupiter Grades serves as our Learning Management System. As a uniform school, we promote community and belonging. City Year enriches student life through after-school programs and family resources. We partner with Mount Sinai Hospital for a fully-equipped medical clinic with doctor and nurse services. We celebrate diversity and foster a respectful environment where all students and community members feel valued and heard. Learn more at joininms.com

overview: At CIS 303, we will strive to provide a safe environment where all members of the community will be held accountable for the success of each member through efficient structures and clear expectations. We provide learning experiences which develop the learner's passion for the awareness of his or her own learning - we do this through large structures like our Advisory Program, Social Emotional Learning, Anti-Bullying/Isolation, and Digital Citizenship lessons, and with presentations from community-based organizations (like Sandy Hook Promise). We have chosen to enter candidacy to become an International Baccalaureate school to ensure our students will not only have the rigorous education to be high school / college and career ready, but globally minded to accept and attract opportunities wherever they chose. We will utilize this passion for learning and educate the whole person by providing a wide variety of academic challenges (remedial or extension) and expose the student to diverse, non-academic activities: Culture Day, Career Day, Leadership Day, participation in plays through Disney Jr., clubs / after schools, and regular field trips showing students that New York City, not just the four walls of our building, can be their classroom. We improve staff practice and student performance through consistent reflection, feedback and evaluation meeting weekly on Wednesday afternoons for extended professional development. Finally, 303 creates an accessible learning environment where effort is recognized and celebrated as well as achievement, and members are encouraged to do their best.

overview:
At the School for Math, Science and Technology through Art, students thrive in a vibrant, interdisciplinary environment where academic achievement, creativity, and character development go hand in hand. We blend rigorous instruction in math and science with a strong emphasis on the arts, fostering a learning experience that is both challenging and deeply enriching. As an Outward Bound school, we believe that students are crew, not passengerstaking ownership of their learning, supporting one another, and rising to meet challenges together. This mindset is embedded in everything we do, encouraging leadership, collaboration, and personal growth.We consider New York City an extension of our classroom. Students regularly engage in rich, curriculum-connected class trips to museums, science centers, theaters, and historic sites. Our annual trips to Broadway productions and other cultural institutions provide real world context and inspiration, making learning more relevant and meaningful. Our partnership with Broadway Jr. provides students with exciting opportunities to explore the world of theater. They don't just watch, they perform and have taken the stage in full scale productions of Moana, Aladdin, and Mean Girls, building confidence, creativity, and teamwork.Academically, we prepare students for success by offering opportunities to take the New York State Regents Exams in Algebra and Living Environment (Biology), laying a strong foundation for high school achievement.
What truly sets us apart is our commitment to developing the whole child. Through an inclusive, supportive, and inspiring school culture, we nurture character, confidence, and pride.

overview:
Shell Bank Middle School, located in Sheepshead Bay, is a vibrant educational institution committed to providing a well-rounded education 
We celebrate cultural diversity, creating an inclusive environment where every student can discover and develop their unique strengths while promoting a love for learning. We offer a educational experience that embraces innovative programs that foster a culture of curiosity, exploration, and creativity, allowing every student to discover and develop their unique strengths while promoting a love for learning.Infinity at Shell Bank- District 22 Screened Program for Advanced LearnersShell Bank features the Infinity program, the only screened advanced learners' program in District 22, designed to expand learning opportunities beyond the regular curriculum. Our Infinity program offers a rigorous academic curriculum paired with immersive learning opportunities, focusing on critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration. Students engage in real-world experiences and hands-on projects, supported by expert guidance. The Infinity program offers students accelerated classes, providing access to Regents courses such as Algebra 1, Living Environment, Social Studies and English Regents, enabling them to advance their academic achievements and prepare for high school. Students also explore music, dance, art, technology, Chinese language, and specialized high school preparation. Recognized by prestigious schools like Hunter H.S., Infinity prepares students for high academic achievements and future success. Join us at Infinity to see your child thrive in an environment that values learning, creativity, and excellence.

overview: Our mission at M.S. 50, Magnet School for Debate and Youth Leadership, is to empower student voice through debate in all content areas and to promote youth leadership through academics, arts, athletics, and activism. We are proud to be city-wide debate champions and to be ranked in the top 4 in middle school debate in the entire country! At MS 50, all students take advanced Regents classes, and we offer free SHSAT preparation courses. We also have a dynamic Spanish dual language program and a Spanish language debate program. All Students at MS 50 are also exposed to extensive arts and music programming through our partnership with El Puente, a nationally renowned community human rights organization. We have a highly ranked concert band, a Latin jazz ensemble and a drumline, and we have a vibrant visual arts program that includes massive murals. MS 50 students also select from a variety of enrichment activities (debate, concert band, drumline, robotics, video game design, coding, theater, art, photography, step, guitar, newspaper, dance, sports, chess, and more) during our Expanded Learning Time that runs until 4:00. We offer a free afterschool program in partnership with El Puente that provides programming until 6:00 daily.Check us out at www.ms50.org.

overview:
Booker T. Washington MS54 is located on the Upper West Side of Manhattan. It is distinctive for these reasons: (1) Students with diverse needs which range from acceleration, remediation, special accommodations and language development have a place within the school. There are 12:1:1 c Integrated Co-Teaching classes on every grade level.(2) Every student has the opportunity to take art and music during their middle school years. Our music department includes piano, chorus, strings, and band classes. We also offer French, Spanish, Latin, and Mandarin. (3) Students are provided with additional academic support before and after school through teacher office hours. During this same time, students are able to meet with their teachers in small groups. (4) The school has a science lab, 2 computer labs, and a library media center has a collection of over 30,000 and is staffed by a full-time librarian. The school has high expectations for the students and emphasizes academic achievement, strong character, and hard work. An extensive extra-curricular program has included student council, newspaper club, debate club, math team, robotics, crafts, art, band, music creation. The sports program includes boys and girls and varsity and JV sport, in addition to softball, baseball, table tennis, ultimate frisbee, and flag football. Boys and Girls Basketball Teams, Track Team, Art Portfolio Program, Music Enrichment, Math Team, Model United Nations and Drama Program. overview: Louis Pasteur Middle School 67Q offers three programs for incoming students: the Zoned Program, the Screened Program, and the STEM Lottery Program. Students engage in four core academic courses each year, along with STEM coursework in Coding and Robotics and a wide range of electives such as Journalism, Student Voice, Financial Literacy, Informational Literacy, Health, and other enrichment experiences that support a well-rounded education. Students may also select from six arts disciplines-Studio Art, Graphic Art & Design, Theater, Dance, Vocal Music, and Instrumental Music-to complete a three-year sequence that nurtures creativity and self-expression. Academic progress is closely monitored, and based on performance in Grades 6 and 7, students may access accelerated or double-accelerated pathways leading to Regents-level coursework in Mathematics, Science, and Social Studies, as well as the Spanish Language Proficiency assessment. Beyond the classroom, students benefit from a free, on-site after-school program in partnership with the Samuel Field Y and can participate in more than 30 clubs, teams, and activities across all seasons. Through comprehensive social-emotional supports, including counseling services, team-based lessons, and assemblies, MS 67Q ensures every child is known and supported. overview: At MS 88, every student is known, valued, and inspired. We are a welcoming, innovative middle school where students discover their passions, develop their voice, and build the confidence and skills for future success. Beginning in Fall 2026, MS 88 launches a redesigned middle school experience that combines rigorous academics, student choice, and real-world learning within smaller learning communities where students develop meaningful relationships, a strong sense of belonging, and the personalized support to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. All sixth graders begin in our Discovery Academy, a supportive transition program focused on executive functioning, organization, leadership, and independence while exploring both the Creative Conservatory (Arts) and Innovation Institute (STEM) through immersive electives and project-based learning. At the end of sixth grade, students choose a pathway that aligns with their interests. The Creative Conservatory nurtures artistic expression through visual arts, music, theater, and performance, while the Innovation Institute immerses students in coding, robotics, engineering, artificial intelligence, health sciences, digital media, and design thinking. Across all grades, students develop critical thinking, communication, collaboration, creativity, and leadership through authentic learning, capstone experiences, and community partnerships. With accelerated coursework, comprehensive supports, and exceptional programs in athletics, robotics, theater, music, visual arts, and student leadership, MS 88 empowers every learner to become an innovative thinker, compassionate leader, and engaged citizen prepared to thrive in high school, college, careers, and beyond.

overview: At Michelangelo Junior High School 144, students embark on a journey toward academic excellence and personal growth. Through a rigorous curriculum aligned with the Next Generation Learning Standards, our students develop into critical thinkers, effective problem solvers, thoughtful decision makers, and compassionate, ethical citizens. We take pride in preparing students for the academic demands of high school and beyond. Our dedicated Parent Association working closely with the parent coordinator ensures strong home-school communication and fosters a vibrant school community. Together, they support a variety of events, including student celebrations, theatrical productions, concerts, Honor Roll breakfasts, Academic Parent Teacher Team Evenings,Honor Society Night, and Family Nights. Families stay engaged with their child's learning through tools like Google Classroom, APTT, and the family newsletter where they can track academic progress and upcoming assignments. We also host Academic Parent-Teacher Team meetings six times a year, offering opportunities for families to collaborate directly with educators and students. With more than 30 student clubs, Michelangelo Junior High School 144 offers a dynamic range of opportunities for students to engage meaningfully both during the school day and in after-school programs. These clubs foster personal interests, leadership skills, and a strong sense of community, enriching the overall student experience. Our guidance counselors provide personalized support throughout the high school admissions process, and we are proud that our graduates have earned acceptance into many of New York City's specialized high schools, as well as music schools, art schools, and fashion schools.

overview:
At IS 162, we recognize that students learn best when they feel safe, supported, and connected. ur middle school is a place where students thrive academically, socially, and emotionally in a nurturing, inclusive, and engaging environment. With a strong emphasis on academic excellence, character development, and community engagement, we are committed to preparing every student for success in high school, college, careers, and beyond.
IS 162 is equipped with modern classrooms, science laboratories, makerspaces, and a thriving hydroponics grow lab that allow students to explore, create, investigate, and innovate. Our college and career readiness programming, supported by our counseling department, helps students set goals, plan for the future, and develop the skills needed for long-term success.
Our comprehensive Social-Emotional Learning program helps students develop self-awareness, empathy, responsible decision-making, and positive relationships. Through student government, leadership opportunities, community service projects, and schoolwide initiatives, students learn the importance of collaboration, responsibility, and making a positive impact on their school and community.
At IS 162, we are proud to foster a school community where students are encouraged to be curious, confident, compassionate, and committed to excellence. Together, we continue to teach the will-to-be excellent.

Students benefit from a nurturing and supportive environment in which a dedicated team of administrators, counselors, and deans remains with each cohort from sixth through eighth grade, providing continuity, guidance, and personalized support throughout their middle school journey. Our rigorous academic program is complemented by nationally recognized opportunities in the arts: a well-developed Fine Arts curriculum includes Band, Chorus, and Visual Arts, and through partnerships with organizations such as the Queens Arts Festival, our Visual Arts students have earned top honors at the Queens Borough Arts Festival, with award-winning work displayed at the Queens Museum. We take pride in fostering student voice, leadership, and critical thinking; through our partnership with MSQI, students participate in one of New York City’s top-ranked middle school debate programs. Our commitment to academic excellence is further reflected by participation in initiatives such as Urban Advantage, the NY Road Runners Club, and the NYC Public Schools College Access for All program, which helps students develop college awareness and readiness beginning in seventh grade to support informed decision-making as they transition to high school. Recognizing the importance of social-emotional well-being, families may choose to enroll their children in the South Asian Youth Action (SAYA!) after-school program, which provides additional academic, social, and emotional support, and our faculty and staff also offer an extensive after-school enrichment program.

overview: At Middel School 217 we will foster integrity, reflection, critical thinking, kindness, and responsibility for others. overview:
Montauk Junior High School: Empowering Future Leaders in a Diverse and Nurturing Environment
Montauk Junior High School is a vibrant, inclusive learning community serving approximately 650 students who represent over 17 languages. Our small school environment allows us to provide personalized attention and foster strong relationships between students, teachers, and families. With a low student-to-teacher ratio and a commitment to academic excellence, we are proud to offer a wide range of programs that challenge and support our diverse learners.
Academic Excellence and Opportunity
Montauk JHS provides a robust academic program, including accelerated and Regents-level courses. Students in select classes take Algebra and Biology, with over 95% of students passing these Regents exams annually. As the host site for District Algebra Honors and Superintendent Classes, we provide accelerated pathways for students to earn high school credits in 8th grade. These include Regents exams in Algebra, Biology, U.S. History, and the Language Proficiency Exam in Mandarin.
We are also proud to offer the AVID program, a nationally recognized college and career readiness initiative, which equips students with essential study skills and prepares them for rigorous coursework in high school and beyond.
Real-World Readiness: Financial Literacy and Civics for All
In preparing students for life beyond the classroom, Montauk JHS prioritizes Financial Literacy and Civics Education for all students. Our curriculum includes dedicated instruction in money management, budgeting, and financial responsibility, ensuring that every student gains essential life skills. Additionally, through the Civics for All initiative, students engage in meaningful exploration of civic duties.

overview: JHS 226 Virgil I. Grissom is a learning community that focuses on the academic, social, and emotional growth of all students. The school is organized into three learning communities. Sixth grade students join our community as members of the Discovery and Explorations Academy. Students in 7th and 8th grade are members of the Humanities Academy and Renaissance Academy, respectively. Students at each grade level participate in rigorous, hands-on learning experiences that provide them with opportunities to explore new content, make connections to real-world situations, and develop arguments to support new ideas. A well-rounded education is the cornerstone of our academic program, and students participate in a variety of elective courses. These include visual arts, dance, theatre, band, technology, health, and Virtual Enterprise Junior Venture in which students develop a virtual business. All students take part in an advisory class, which supports social-emotional growth. Advanced Regents Program (ARP/Honors) classes are offered, and Regents exams in Algebra, Biology, and World Languages are administered. We host a wide variety of extracurricular activities, which are refined each year based on the interests of our current students. In the past, these have included sports programs, academic support and enrichment classes, art club, a dance partnership with Alvin Ailey, band, and E-Sports. Students also have an opportunity to sign-up for after-school programs through Beacon or Opus Theatre and Dance, which run daily until 5:30 pm. These organizations offer additional program options, including karate, aviation, cooking, and tutoring.

overview: William McKinley IS 259, a Title 1 middle school in Brooklyn Bay Ridge, serves grades 6-8 with rigorous academics including screened Independent Investigations Method (IIM) and Virtual Enterprises Junior Ventures (VEJV) programs, a Mandarin Dual Language program, and Regents-tracked coursework in Algebra, Living Environment, and U.S. History available to all students. Acceptance into the Virtual Enterprise and/or Independent Investigations Method programs will limit a student's scheduling options for certain other electives. However, we offer nearly all electives after school (and many before school) for students who do not have room in their daytime schedule but still wish to participate. Students benefit from two upgraded air-conditioned gyms, Promethean Interactive Boards and laptops in every classroom, state-of-the-art auditorium lighting and sound, and hands-on science labs with major upgrades. The school offers a robust Visual and Performing Arts program, including Advanced String Orchestra and Marching Band, along with a wide range of extracurriculars such as robotics, culinary arts, sports, student government, and leadership clubs. McKinley emphasizes social-emotional wellness and community engagement through after-school programs, parent involvement, and partnerships with local organizations, preparing students to be bilingual, biliterate, and bicultural global citizens ready for high school and beyond. See more on social media: Instagram @259events

overview:
At Margaret S. Douglas JHS 292 we launch future LEADERS! Our goal is to develop our scholars into leaders by providing them with education that prepares them for success in high school, college and beyond. Our teachers work collaboratively to ensure that students are provided instruction based on their individual needs. We strive to meet the academic, cultural and social needs of our scholars by providing them with rigorous instruction in all content areas that is culturally relevant. In addition we engage in social emotional learning with restorative practices embedded throughout our community. We have a Specialized High School program called LEADERS offered to all students that gives them the opportunity to prepare for the Specialized High Schooltest therefore giving them anopportunity to attend specialized high schools. As a result of attending our Leaders program many of our students pass the test and attend Stuyvesant High School, Brooklyn Latin HS, and Brooklyn Technical High School. We also have students that are acceptedthrough a rigorous application process to Bard Early College HS. 
 Our seventh and eighth grade scholars are afforded the opportunity to prepare for and take Regents exams in Algebra 1; Biology ; and US History . Over 90% of our scholars who take theregents exam pass with a 90% or higher rate which earns them accelerated high school credit. We also offer performing arts classes such as Dance, Culinary Arts, Music/Band,Fitness, Drama/Theaterand Film Making.

overview: John Ericsson Middle School 126, located in the Greenpoint section of Brooklyn is a diverse, vibrant learning environment comprised of passionate and resilient students and staff. Our mission is to ensure that every student develops the skills necessary to build a strong social and academic foundation that leads to a productive and informed citizen who can communicate and collaborate with a diverse community. With our partnerships with St. Nicks Alliance, and participation in initiatives such as STEAM, College Access for All, Algebra for All, Civics for All, and Computer Science for All, our students are provided with world-class learning opportunities and experiences that support our students in becoming civic-minded leaders. Our students fly drones, build futuristic heliports, program robots with their coding skills, test the soil and water quality, use the school garden and Hydroponics Lab to study vegetation, and create simple machines for presentation at our Annual STEAM Expo. Our students participate in advisory groups, engage in daily class discussion, weekly class debates, meet CEOs of corporations, redesign neighborhood parks to be environmentally-friendly, and work in small groups to strengthen their reading and math skills. Monthly trips to museums, parks, cultural institutions and colleges provide students with real world applications to what they learn and design in school.Our students are building community to engineer the future.

overview: Welcome to Juan Morel Campos, where academic excellence, creativity, and college readiness are at the heart of everything we do. Serving students in grades 6-12, we foster a culture of high expectations and provide the support necessary for every student to achieve success. Our comprehensive educational program combines rigorous academics with rich artistic opportunities, ensuring students develop both critical thinking skills and creative talents. Through theater, digital arts, filmmaking, band, dance, and other arts programs, students are encouraged to explore their passions and express themselves in meaningful ways. Preparing students for college and future careers begins early at Juan Morel Campos. Starting in 6th grade, our college-bound initiative helps students build the skills, confidence, and mindset needed for higher education. With the guidance of a full-time college counselor and a dedicated team of educators, students receive personalized support throughout their academic journey. Beyond the classroom, students can participate in a wide range of extracurricular activities, including coding, cooking, debate, guitar, student council, STEM programs, peer mediation, and Saturday Academy. Our athletic programs in basketball, baseball, soccer, handball, and softball promote teamwork, leadership, and healthy competition. At Juan Morel Campos, we are proud to be a caring, inclusive community that welcomes and celebrates students from all backgrounds. Together, we create a supportive environment where every student can grow, achieve, and thrive academically, artistically, and personally.

overview:
KAPPA V recognizes that each child is an individual who is creative and can succeed. We believe that all students are capable of learning, and we work to develop the social, academic, and intellectual habits that will inspire them to become tomorrow s leaders. KAPPA V is a college and career-ready school that provides rigorous instruction and exposure to college and university life for both our students and their families. This is made possible through our interactive curriculum, college tours, and workshops.
Our school has made significant academic gains, with a 22% increase in our ELA state exam scores last year. We continue to prioritize literacy because we know that if students can read and comprehend, they can master any subject. To give our students a competitive edge, 8th-grade students can earn high school credits by taking the Algebra I and Living Environment Regents exams.
We offer a wide range of academic and enrichment programs: STEM Program: A hallmark of our school, our STEM program includes project-based learning, hands-on science projects, drone photography, and flight aviation. Computer Science for All: This initiative exposes our students to careers in computer science through robotics, game/program design, and more. Arts Partnerships: Through partnerships with Opus Dance Theatre and Broadway Junior, students can explore dance, photography, steel pan, marching band, majorettes, choir, chess, and drama. Extended Day Program: Our program runs until 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, offering academic intervention, sports, trips, and various arts and STEM programs.
We also ensure our scholars have two electronic devices (one for school and one for home) and have a dedicated social-emotional learning curriculum to help them navigate middle school life.

overview: Located in the heart of Far Rockaway, Queens, Knowledge and Power Preparatory Academy VI (KAPPA VI) is a small, inclusive, and tight-knit learning community where every student is known, supported, and challenged. Modeled after the Air Force philosophy of leadership and service, our students, called cadets, are encouraged to lead with integrity, think critically, and aim high. Each class, known as a squadron, is named after a NASA space mission, and our students wear uniforms that reflect pride, purpose, and unity. At KAPPA VI, our vision is to be an Ivy League Middle School Academy, preparing cadets not just for high school, but for lifelong success in college, career, and civic life. Our rigorous academic program includes opportunities for students to earn high school credit through Regents-level coursework in Algebra I, Biology, U.S history and Spanish Language Proficiency. Our cadets are also encouraged to take the Specialized High School Admissions Test (SHSAT) to broaden their access to top-tier high school options. Beyond the classroom, we are proud to offer a wide range of enrichment experiences that allow students to explore their passions and talents in areas such as Urban Agriculture, Food Science, Engineering, Journalism, Robotics, Chess, and Musical Theater. Our robust arts program includes general music, visual art, guitar, and band, supporting the development of the whole child. Every cadet has daily access to Chromebooks, and our staff integrates technology through Google Classroom to support interactive, student-centered learning. We are equally committed to our students' social and emotional growth, by ensuring our cadets meet with our guidance counselor and social worker on a regular basis.

overview: Lafayette Academy is a rising star in District 3 and one of Manhattan's most promising small middle schools. With an intimate student body of approximately 200 students, Lafayette offers a close-knit, nurturing community where every child is known, valued, and challenged. Our highly dedicated and passionate faculty are among the most dynamic educators in New York City, creating rigorous, engaging, and inclusive learning experiences that support each student's academic, emotional, and social growth. At Lafayette, we take pride in our unique ability to balance strong academics with a warm, student-centered environment. Our school's size allows us to build deep, meaningful relationships with our students and families, ensuring that every child is both supported and pushed to achieve their personal best. We are proud to be home to the only French Dual Language Program in Manhattan, offering bilingual students and native French speakers continued access to French language arts and selected content-area instruction in French. This program enriches our school community and cultivates global citizenship among our students. Understanding the significant developmental transitions that occur during the middle school years, we are deeply committed to preparing our students for the academic and social challenges of high school and beyond. Our graduates go on to some of the city's most competitive high schools, including Stuyvesant, Bronx Science, Brooklyn Tech, Bard, Beacon, LaGuardia, the NYC iSchool, and many more. At Lafayette Academy, we don't just educate students we empower them to lead, inspire, and thrive.

Our vision is to instill a love for learning by placing the learner at the center of everything we do in order to promote self-confidence, thoughtful decision-making, and academic and social growth. We provide a positive and supportive learning environment that challenges students to think, explore, and create as they connect rigorous academic experiences with robust arts education while including choices such as sports and computer science. At Legacy School of the Arts, students receive individualized instruction whether they are learning disabled or a part of our Gifted and Talented program. Legacy students are exposed to a variety of the arts in grade 6, such as visual art, dance, theater (including a Broadway show), and music. In grades 7 and 8, our students will focus their study on an art of their choosing to further develop their individual skills. At Legacy School of the Arts, we believe that social-emotional development is as important as academic development; all students will be part of a small group advisory led by their mentor. We encourage our students to be future oriented and mindful of their impact on the world. At LSA, we ask ourselves daily: "What's Your Legacy?"

overview: Lenox Academy M.S. 961 is an academically accelerated program for middle school students. We provide a high-quality education in a small, loving and supportive environment. Lenox Academy's rigorous academic program, coupled with a highly skilled and experienced staff, has proven successful, as nearly all of our 8th great students confidently sit for three Regents exams and the Spanish Proficiency Exam. At Lenox, our motto is "Find your passion ~ Find your voice." Through our Electives classes, students are able to experience enrichment in areas they are passionate about during the school day. Through our robust student government, and our advisory program, which allows students to give regular input on school decisions, students develop their unique voices. Lenox Academy promotes academic excellence and challenges students to meet NYS standards with distinction. Our seniors are administered the English Language Arts and Algebra I Common Core Regents, Biology Regents and Spanish World Language exams. The arts and athletics are also very important to Lenox.We have an after school partner in New York Edge that offers free after school with arts and sports.We partner with Brooklyn Conservatory of Music for our band.Students get Visual Arts and Music classes over their time at Lenox and we have a Step team.We put on a big play each year with Broadway Jr. which all students can be a part of.We have boys basketball, girls basketball, co-ed soccer and boys and girls track teams. We have a large cheerleading teams which competes successfully in tournaments around the city, and we host our own cheer festival. We want our students to be able to try as many experiences as possible so they can find their passion in life and grow their voices over their time at Lenox.

overview: Lower Manhattan Community (LMC) is a small, rigorous middle school with a strong arts program that serves a diverse community. Over the three years of middle school, we aim to challenge students to think creatively, solve problems, and, most importantly, engage with their peers to build connections and share ideas and experiences. At LMC, students take four arts courses: Digital Arts, Dance, Music, and Visual Arts. They have the opportunity to engage with the art course that resonates with them the most. Every Wednesday after lunch, our students participate in a small advisory group of 10-12 of their peers. Led by one of their teachers, our advisory curriculum explores topics such as goal-setting, identity, values, service, and human rights. These advisories provide a framework for the numerous field trips, including overnight trips, that our students participate in throughout the year. In advisory, we also prepare students for the opportunity of 'out lunch', which students in good academic standing are eligible for after the first trimester of 6th grade. At LMC, our robust after-school program, developed in partnership with Manhattan Youth, builds on our arts, academic, and advisory programs through daily programming that is free of charge.

overview:
Lyons Community School is a small, public middle and high school in Brooklyn serving grades 6-12. With intentionally small class sizes, Lyons is designed for students who thrive when they are known well, supported deeply, and challenged meaningfully.
Learning at Lyons is personal and purposeful. Students build strong academic skills, explore real-world interests, and develop into confident, thoughtful young adults. Our close-knit environment allows teachers to work closely with students and families to support both academic growth and social-emotional development.
Lyons provides comprehensive special education services, including Integrated Co-Teaching (ICT), individualized accommodations, and targeted supports aligned to students’ IEPs. Special education teachers collaborate with classroom teachers and support staff to ensure students with diverse learning needs are challenged and successful.
We also offer strong support for English Language Learners, with dedicated language instruction and integrated support within content-area classes. English learners are full members of the school community and are supported to build academic language, confidence, and independence.
As a member of the New York State Performance Standards Consortium, Lyons uses Performance-Based Assessment Tasks (PBATs) instead of most Regents exams (only the ELA Regents is required). Students demonstrate learning through research, experiments, projects, and presentations, building strong writing, critical thinking, and presentation skills.
Learning extends beyond the classroom through internships, weekly field studies, arts, and social justice projects. Through Career Readiness & Modern Youth Apprenticeship (CRMYA) and Future Ready NYC, eligible students access paid internships.

overview: Madiba Prep Middle School of Social Justice and Innovation is a District 16 school serving scholars in grades 6-8. We are a learning community where scholars are steeped in the rigorous pursuit of critical thinking skills, communication and technological literacy, self-awareness, and social and character development. Parents and community stakeholders support the development of scholars who are productive, contributing citizens in the local and global contexts. Our learning projects will position scholars to take the information that they have learned and propose a solution to a real-world problem within their local community and make connections to our global community. Our students have access to Theater, Art, Jazz, Tap, Hip-Hop, Digital Music Production, Fabrication Lab, Fencing, Golf, Archery, and a range of clubs and teams, and national travel opportunities. From video game and APP design to boat making, Botany and Space Camp we offer activities that nurture and stimulate scholars. We offer a warm and caring environment with a variety of learning opportunities that include double period Honors English, Algebra, and Living Environment Regents classes. After-school provides an eclectic mix of activities and academic support.

overview:
P.S. 126/MAT (Jacob Riis School) is a vibrant 3K-8 school in the heart of Chinatown, where a caring community and strong relationships allow teachers to truly know, support, and challenge every child. From our youngest learners through middle school, students thrive in a creative and rigorous academic environment that emphasizes foundational literacy, inquiry, collaboration, public speaking, and social-emotional learning.
Technology is embedded across all core subjects, with hands-on opportunities in computer science, coding, animation, robotics, and STEM. Beginning in 3rd grade, eligible students may participate in our Gifted & Talented program (Grades 3-5). By middle school, all students are prepared to take Biology and Algebra I Regents exams, as well as the Spanish Proficiency exam, ensuring strong high school readiness.
P.S. 126/MAT offers a rich arts and enrichment program, including visual arts, band, percussion, and fine arts majors, along with partnerships with 3rd Street Music, CREA, ArtsWork, and Chess NYC. Students also enjoy swimming, access to outdoor fields, and an extensive competitive athletics program with 23 sports, with 5th graders eligible to participate and receiving priority admission to our middle school.
Our school celebrates the diversity of our community through cultural events and offers afterschool programs, including coding, STEM, dance, and holiday camps. With small class sizes, strong SEL supports, and access to middle school teachers for elementary students, P.S. 126/MAT is a place where children grow into confident, curious, and compassionate learners; ready for success in high school and beyond.

overview: Mark Twain Intermediate School for the Gifted and Talented sets itself apart from others because of its dual mission. Students are immersed in an environment of academic rigor blended with a full visual art and performing arts experience, all in an extremely supportive environment. Twain is organized into clusters, or mini-schools, student are grouped with a team of teachers assigned to each. Clusters are scheduled for conference periods to facilitate interdisciplinary planning, data analysis and communication with parents to discuss student progress. This helps teachers and families strategize and focus their instruction to suit individual student needs. Every child is involved in the in-depth study of a Talent area helping students to hone their skills. Mark Twain has invested in innovative teaching strategies that incorporate technology across all classrooms, promoting the development of 21st century skills.In addition, Mark Twain has embedded the components of Mastery Learning throughout the school community. This approach to learning promotes student progress by through a feedback cycle that focuses on crucial next steps to achieve and deepen mastery of critical skills.

overview: The Metropolitan Expeditionary Learning School, "A School for a Sustainable City", is a NYC Outward Bound School (www.nycoutwardbound.org). We serve grades 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12.MELS offers all students a rigorous college preparatory program, with particular emphasis on sustainability. MELS has been recognized as a Showcase School by the New York City Department of Education and one of ten Mentor Expeditionary Learning schools across the country. The school follows the Expeditionary Learning model (www.eleducation.org), in which students engage in learning expeditions and have multiple opportunities for hands-on learning, both inside and outside of the classroom. Students participate in fieldwork with civic leaders, industry figures, and environmental scientists to examine agriculture, architecture, city infrastructure, design, environmental policy, law, and planning. Our graduates, through their examination of the principles of sustainability, will be equipped with the skills necessary to succeed in college and to guide the new decisions faced by our city and our world.

overview: At the Middle School for Art and Philosophy (MSAP), we believe every student deserves a safe, inclusive, and inspiring learning environment where they are challenged academically, supported socially and emotionally, and empowered to discover their unique talents. The arts are at the heart of who we are. Students explore their creativity through visual arts, dance, theater, chorus, mural design, culinary arts, music production, keyboarding, and more. Throughout the school year, students showcase their talents through multiple school-wide performances and exhibitions, including our annual Art Gala. Our rigorous academic program prepares students for success in high school and beyond through standards-based instruction, targeted academic intervention, and opportunities for advanced coursework, including the Biology and Algebra I Regents. As a restorative practices and Outward Bound school, we believe in elevating student voice, building leadership, developing student advocacy, and creating a strong sense of belonging through meaningful community building experiences.Students develop critical thinking, effective communication, conflict resolution, and peer mediation skills while learning to take responsibility for their actions and contribute positively to their school community. At MSAP, we believe every student has the potential to lead with optimism, accountability, and resilience while making a meaningful impact both inside and outside the classroom. Our goal is to graduate confident, creative, and compassionate young people who are prepared to thrive academically, pursue their passions with purpose, and SOAR as leaders in their schools and communities.

overview: Mott Hall Bridges Academy is a small middle school in Brownsville, Brooklyn. Currently, 200 scholars are enrolled, resulting in a close knit, family environment. Our STEAM focus prepares scholars not only to be independent, critical thinkers, but to be equipped for the challenges of the 21st century. The social emotional development of our scholars is of utmost important to us here at Mott Hall Bridges Academy. Programs such as She Is Me and IMatter are geared towards their personal development. Our Champion program ensures that each scholar has an adult who he/she can confide in or rely on for support. All scholars are assigned to one of our four Houses where the team works to instill a sense of camaraderie through friendly competition. Monthly competitions such as the Spelling Bee, Step Wars, Math Bowl, Poetry Slam and Bridges Got Talent, are some of the ways that we maintain a strong positive culture at our school. Our Be Cool Be Kind anti-bullying campaign and efforts to stamp out bullying has earned us the designation of a Respect For All School. Here at MHBA we have a niche for every scholar. Our Royal Researchers Science Club and our robust Art program allows scholars to nurture their creativity and follow their passion. Students present quarterly performances in our Community Spotlight elective classes. Our Athletic Department is also an active part of what makes our school unique. Our different sports teams include: Royal Vision Steppers, Royal Hitters Softball Team, Royal Knights Basketball (Varsity & JV) Royal Knights Football (Varsity & JV), Royal Runners Track Team, and Royal Rhythm Dance Team.

overview: Mott Hall III is proud to be an International Baccalaureate (IB) World School. This distinction reflects our commitment to a rigorous, inquiry-based curriculum where students think critically, make real-world connections, and develop the habits of character reflected in the IB Learner Profile, including becoming caring, open-minded, and knowledgeable members of their communities. Our students and families value our small, supportive environment where every child is known, cared for deeply, and challenged to reach their highest potential. We celebrate student talents through curriculum fairs, talent showcases, and cultural celebrations. Students explore future pathways through college trips and College and Career Days. Through our partnership with LEAP (Learning through an Expanded Arts Program), students participate in daily afterschool enrichment opportunities. We also offer a variety of athletics, including basketball, flag football, track and field, baseball, softball, soccer, and volleyball. Our musical theater program brings a Broadway-level production to our community each year, and our visual arts program helps students develop their unique artistic expression and portfolios for high school applications. Our eighth graders consistently gain acceptance to top specialized, selective, independent, and parochial high schools throughout NYC and beyond. Students benefit from technology-rich classrooms and opportunities to take Regents-level courses and earn high school credit. At MH3, we partner with families to ensure every student grows as a scholar, artist, athlete, leader, and global citizen. Come see what we have to offeryou will find your future at MH3!

Through rigorous academics and project-based learning, students are empowered to think critically, collaborate effectively, and grow as innovative leaders throughout their middle school journey.

overview: MS 53 offers a warm, student-centered environment in which students enjoy a curriculum of rigorous academics in math and the sciences. Through our challenging coursework, we encourage our students academically while providing a safe and supportive learning environment. A carefully developed, challenging course of study is designed to foster creative and independent thought and facilitate students' success in the top high schools in New York City. At MS 53 our students in the 8th grade take Algebra 1 and Living Environment as well as complete the regents in both courses to begin high school with credits. Teachers are trained in EdTech, and the students are engaged in Virtual Enterprise. Virtual Enterprise is a program that enables students to develop technology and entrepreneurial skills by starting and managing business ventures. Our wide array of extracurricular activities gives students numerous opportunities to engage and excel in community service, cultural arts, athletics, student government, and academic competition and research. Our family-oriented school strives to give back to our community through supports we receive from our strategic partnerships, which include but are not limited to, Child Center and Community Mediation Services that provides a well-rounded extracurricular program for our students. Our scholars have access to numerous in-school and after-school programs that are available through our partnerships which are designed to enrich and compliment their learning style and experiences. At MS 53 our Motto is being our best always, and our graduates become productive members of society, which go on to excel at their high schools of choice as well as college, careers and beyond.

overview:
RELC is an Arts and Technology school located in Fort Greene, Brooklyn, focused on inquiry-based, student-centered instruction and developing well-rounded scholars.We utilize the following curriculums Illustrative Math, Expeditionary Learning in ELA, Amplify Science, and the NYCPS Passport Social Studies curriculum.We currently have 4 classes on each grade level, which includes General Education, Integrated Co-Teaching, Special Education (12:1:1 Self-Contained) and Dual Language Spanish. We also offer a Regents class for high performing students in Grade 8 only (Earth Science regents). 
Additionally, we offer the Arts (either Classical Dance, Vocal Music or Visual Arts), Technology and Spanish language instruction to every students as a part of the regular curriculum.Students are supported through a weekly Social Emotional Learning class, weekly morning meetings (by grade) and an optional Mentoring program.We offer afree, daily afterschool programming through our Community-Based Organization partner, Long Island University.
Our students have the opportunity to participate in our Annual College Tour and visit a variety of cultural institutions and landmarks throughout New York City.
Finally, we strive to provide an environment where every child feels seen, heard and appreciated. Our goal is to ensure that every child has at least one adult resource who they can speak with if they are having a challenge or just need good advice. We encourage families to schedule a visit to our school building to see our staff and students in action and hear from them directly.

overview: At The Academy for Independent Learning and Leadership, we believe that Royalty Resides in the Bronx. Every scholar is recognized as a Young King or Queen whose voice, identity, and potential matter. Our school is a welcoming community where students are challenged academically, supported socially and emotionally, and empowered to lead with confidence. Through rigorous instruction in English Language Arts, mathematics, science, and social studies, students develop the critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills needed for success in high school, college, and beyond. Our scholars also explore their passions through courses and experiences in technology, visual and graphic arts, music, financial literacy, social justice, and leadership development. At The Academy, learning extends beyond the classroom. Students participate in service-learning projects, leadership opportunities, clubs, and community partnerships that help them connect their learning to real-world issues and make a positive impact in their community. Our culture is grounded in our belief that every child deserves to be seen, heard, challenged, and celebrated. Guided by our school pledge"We Are Power. We Are Peace. Stand Up and Speak!"our Young Kings and Queens learn to advocate for themselves, support one another, and lead with purpose. By graduation, students leave The Academy prepared academically, equipped with strong character, and ready to shape their future with confidence. At The Academy for Independent Learning and Leadership, we don't just prepare students for high school-we prepare them to lead.

overview: The Salk School is a small, nurturing community that emphasizes critical thinking skills in a fun, collaborative environment. Our curriculum is designed to value student interest and creativity, tapping into children's natural curiosity and desire to do good in the world while engaging with powerful ideas across disciplines.Over the course of three years, we seek to nurture our students as scientists, writers, historians, artists, mathematicians, and compassionate human beings. We help them develop strong voices, an appreciation for diversity, a sense of responsibility and the passion and resilience to grapple with hard problems. Named after Dr. Jonas Salk, our school is a place where students come to see science as a way of making sense of the natural world through observation, experimentation, and an open and critical exchange of ideas. Salk students leave appreciating that science, ideally, is humanity's attempt to make the world better for all living things and to ensure the health of our planet.

overview:
MS 267 Math, Science & Technology
School Overview At MS 267 Math, Science & Technology, we believe that all scholars can learn and all scholars want to learn. Our school community is dedicated to providing a safe, supportive, and academically rigorous environment where scholars are challenged to reach their full potential while developing the skills necessary for success in high school, college, and beyond. Mission Statement The MS 267 community will work relentlessly to empower our scholars to be successful in high school, college, and beyond. Our Commitment We are committed to fostering academic excellence, leadership, creativity, and social-emotional growth through engaging instruction, meaningful relationships, and enriching experiences both inside and outside the classroom. Our scholars participate in rigorous standards-based learning while developing critical thinking, collaboration, communication, and problem-solving skills. Learning Beyond the Classroom At MS 267, learning extends far beyond our school walls. Scholars participate in educational and cultural experiences that broaden their perspectives and expose them to new opportunities. Throughout the year, scholars attend Broadway productions, museums, colleges, cultural institutions, STEM experiences, and other destinations based on their interests and aspirations. These experiences help scholars make real-world connections to their learning while exploring future college and career pathways. Student Leadership Student voice is an important part of our school culture. Each year, our Student Government is elected and formally installed in early October. Student leaders work collaboratively with staff and peers to organize events, represent scholar concerns, and contribute to school-wide initiatives.

overview: As a college-preparatory middle school, Luisa Dessus Cruz, Middle School 302 is dedicated to the academic and personal development of students who will become tomorrow's leaders in the fields of mathematics, science, technology, and social service. Our curriculum develops well-rounded students who are challenged and engaged. The teachers are readying students to creatively and critically think, become self-disciplined, and develop social responsibility through high quality driven instruction. Students are challenged to question, problem-solve, communicate, and assume personal responsibility. We are an empowering and nurturing school community of diverse and collaborative members dedicated to achieving high standards for all of our students. Before our students graduate, it is expected that our students visit a minimum of 10 colleges and complete 30 hours of community service. Our students are afforded Latin percussion, modern dance, music production, visual arts, and coding. Our students participate in basketball, track and field, volleyball, flag football, cheerleading, and tennis. Our partnerships include: NY Historical Society, CHAMPS, Sophie Gerson Healthy Youth, Urban Advantage, Bronx Ensemble, and National Dance Institute.

overview: MS 319 is a vibrant and inclusive learning community committed to empowering students academically, socially, and emotionally. Our mission is to equip students with the tools for intellectual and personal growth while inspiring them to become active, engaged learners who challenge injustice and advocate for a more equitable and inclusive global community. At MS 319, we cultivate a safe and supportive environment where every student feels valued and inspired. Through strong relationships, students develop independence, confidence, and critical problem-solving skills. We have a deep emphasis on rigorous academic learning, meaningful digital engagement, extracurricular opportunities, and active participation in both school and community life, ensuring that students grow into compassionate, informed individuals. Our instructional practices are grounded in deep learning and real-world application. Across all subject areas, students engage in in-depth text analysis and extended writing, strengthening literacy while making meaningful connections to global issues. Our instructional approach integrates scientific inquiry, digital literacy, and critical thinking through experiential, project-based learning, preparing students to think deeply and contribute thoughtfully to the world around them.

overview: MS324 is a school where students and their families are supported in achieving academic and socio-emotional success. Principal Carlos Guzman was raised just four blocks from Patria Mirabal and is very much aware of the challenges that students face on a daily basis. This separates Patria from many of the other schools as their leader is a product of the environment and has his heart set on making Patria a school where all students feel valued, safe and all of their academic needs are met. Patria Mirabal has a staff that goes above and beyond for their students. Teachers are extremely dedicated, professional and competent in their craft. Teachers do not leave Patria Mirabal and it is a place where they would send their own children. Patria Mirabal offers a variety of programs before and after school for students. Programs include Art, Music, Stem, Theatre and many more. Academically, students have the opportunity to graduate with High School credits in Living Environment and Algebra I, and many students are accepted into the specialized High Schools around the city. Using restorative practices and approaches, our staff is equipped to provide a wealth of emotional support for our students no matter what they are experiencing.

overview: At Middle School 390, we offer a variety of exciting and engaging extracurricular activities which keep our students actively involved, promoting equity and inclusiveness. The school culture emphasizes student social-emotional development and leadership. Students are empowered to make positive decisions through the 7 Habits of Highly Effective People- Leader in Me process; thus fostering student engagement and leadership skills. Additionally, we foster strong relationships with families, maintaining consistent communication about student progress and open monthly parents meetings. Each class is 100% equipped with Apple technology (one-to-one iPad and laptop). We are part of the Middle School Quality Initiative, our students have access to state-of-the art technology such as, (Veative/ Virtual Reality set) which provides students with opportunity to interact and engage with their subjects in a virtual reality environment. In addition, we offer dual language and transitional bilingual programs in English and Spanish, Pre- Regents, Regents, and Specialized High School Prep Programs. These programs are designed to provide students with the opportunity to participate in Regents courses in the eighth grade (Algebra and Living Environment) and two years of Specialized High School Prep. Thus, maximizing opportunities for college and career readiness. Students are committed to engage in rigorous curricula and participate in high school and college prep programs (Cornell University-Juntos Program, Lehman College, Gear Up Thrives, Bronx Community college -TRIO and Liberty Programs).

overview: Students enjoy an inclusive and engaging, learning environment, supported by experienced faculty. We provide our students with an honors program, including Algebra, Biology, U.S. History & Government & English regents in grade 8. Our program offers a three-year, in-depth study of drama, instrumental music, dance chorus, art or photography. Students can study Chinese, French or Spanish over two to three year Accelerated Language and Culture course, preparing them for the High School Proficiency exam. Social-emotional supports include three guidance counselors and two social workers, and our after school enrichment and leadership programs. The MS51 student government consists of class mayors, a school president, vice-president and congress. Our social emotional, academic and artistic programs prepare our students for the best high schools in NYC! Over 85% of our 8th graders are matched to one of their top choices. Parents have a strong voice in the School Leadership Team and Parent Association, fundraising and volunteering opportunities. Our captive lunch allows student to use the outdoor campus to recharge. Our students also enjoy overnight trips, field trips, and community service opportunities. overview: M.S. 582, located in East Williamsburg, Brooklyn, is The Magnet School for Multimedia Technology and Urban Planning, serving students in grades 6-8. Grounded in our philosophy of Experience, Exposure, and Discovery, we provide students with meaningful opportunities to explore their interests and develop the skills needed for future success. Beyond our strong core curriculum, students have access to specialized programs in multimedia technology, urban planning, hydroponics, visual arts, music, fabrication, and computer science. Through partnerships with organizations such as Beam Center, BRIC Arts Media, Make: STEAM, NY Sun Works, and Drone Cadets, students engage in hands-on learning experiences that connect classroom learning to the real world. Our extracurricular offerings foster creativity, leadership, and collaboration through activities such as debate, chess, robotics, drones, videography, podcasting, dance, drumline, crochet, and culinary arts. We take pride in our state-of-the-art Fab Lab, equipped with 3D printers, engravers, laser cutters, and digital design tools. Eighth-grade students may challenge themselves through advanced coursework, including Algebra I Regents, Biology Regents, and U.S. History Regents. M.S. 582 also offers a comprehensive athletics and performance program, including baseball, softball, flag football, basketball, volleyball, track and field, wrestling, soccer, kickball, and dance. As a proud Community School, we partner with Grand Street Settlement to provide counseling, family support, and social-emotional services, while St. Nicks Alliance operates our five-day-a-week after-school program. Together, these partnerships ensure that students and families receive the academic, social, and emotional supports needed.

overview: Middle School 890 is a small, tight-knit learning community of just over 300 students that is geared toward student-centered learning and preparation for the real-world through the School-wide Enrichment Model (SEM). Our students are part of one of four academies: Politics & Law, Visual & Performing Arts, Medical & Biological Sciences, and Business, Economics, & Industries. These academies provide a focused enrichment experience throughout their time at MS890. We also offer a range of studio classes that cultivate diverse skills and inspire new interests. Some of our enrichment course offerings include: Urban Agriculture, Genetics, Food Science, Journalism, Chess, Criminal Law, Robotics, Finance, Debate, and Musical Theater. Students have the opportunity of taking advanced courses resulting in regents exams and high school credits, including Algebra 1, Living Environment and Spanish Language Proficiency. Students have a daily advisory period to focus on social-emotional development in a small group setting. We have a robust arts program that includes dance, theater, general music, violin, guitar, band and visual art. Through partnerships with community organizations, students have the opportunity to explore their interests in a fun and engaging environment - which is evidenced by one of the highest attendance rates in the district and city and above-average scores on New York State ELA and Math exams.

overview: At MS 915, we celebrate our diversity and provide students with a voice. This can be seen through our student government body. Our students work collaboratively to solve real life problems. The school utilizes Restorative Justice practices to resolve any behavior concerns. All grades receive visual arts class. 7th and 8th graders receive Spanish instruction several times a week. All students are given advisory periods where they can monitor their academic progress and receive guidance from their advisors. During these periods, advisors also support any social-emotional concerns for students. Twice a year, students engage in an explorations unit where they conduct inquiry based research around a topic of interest. For example, the 6th graders have researched, "What is courage?" Students engage in workshops around the topic, take field trips, and experience guest speakers who are professional experts in the fields of study. Culminating group projects are completed and presented to parents during our Explorations Expo. All students participate in our school's science fair, which is supported through our affiliation with Urban Advantage. All 8th graders have the opportunity to take the Living Environment and Algebra regents courses. Students from low-income households and students in temporary housing have an admissions priority for 57% of seats at this school.

overview: M.S. 935 is the new STEM Middle School in District 19.At M.S. 935, students will explore the world in which they live and work to make it better through Science, Technology, Engineering and Math. STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Math) is an inter-disciplinary style of learning that is student-centered, and project based.Students at M.S. 935 will learn by doing through scientific inquiry, the Engineering Design Process, and innovation skills. The curriculum provides practice in problem solving, discovery exploration, and collaboration, facilitating student understanding of real-world applications of science and engineering. We emphasize design and creativity to give students the freedom to apply critical thinking and cross disciplinary tools, in order to ask questions and solve problems that relate to the world they live in. Using the engineering-design process, students identify problems, design possible solutions, and test and evaluate those solutions. This process, combined with the study of math and science, helps students to find connections that make science, math and technology relevant to their lives and engaging for them.

overview: The mission of Dual Language Middle School (DLMS) is to support a dual language instructional model which promotes academic excellence and is built upon student strengths and curiosities. We believe that students who love languages can learn best through the dual language structure. Students are encouraged to question, challenge, make real decisions, and work collaboratively to solve problems. Through a rigorous project-directed, theme-based curriculum, children learn that school is a place to develop respect for self and others. Our mission is founded on the premise that we must experience an atmosphere of trust, safety, security, and personal attention in order to develop emotional and intellectual growth. At DLMS, each student is assigned an advisor to help them and their families navigate the middle school experiences. Our students take overnight trips to Camp Manice, visit universities like New York University and Fordham, and have mentors from Salesforce and the National Basketball Association to support their growth and development. In addition to core academic classes, all students take 3 years of Spanish, Visual Arts, Physical Education and Dance, with at least two public dance performances per year.Bienvenidos a DLMS!

overview: Follow your own path. Reach new heights. The scholar experience at New Heights Middle School (NHMS) is driven by innovation and technology. Scholars become critical thinkers and problem-solvers through practice in differentiated, real-world experiences and participate in computer science courses across all grade levels. NHMS seeks academic excellence through a rigorous 21st century curriculum coupled with realistic problem-solving and advisement in a safe, caring environment. Through opportunities to engage in meaningful learning in the areas of science, technology, the arts, and math (S.T.E.A.M.) we make active participation in the global community a reality. The teachers and staff of New Heights Middle School are committed to ensuring that all scholars are engaged in rigorous and engaging work and have the opportunity to apply to an Honors Academy. New Heights Middle School partners with various organizations throughout the school year to monitor scholar progress and implement necessary academic interventions. New Heights Middle School is proud to offer unique opportunities that will enhance your child's academic experience through enrichment, after school programming, and extended learning time. These experiences include an award winning FIRST Lego League Robotics Team, Publishing Club, science, and arts-based programming!

overview: New Pathways Arts Academy (NPA) is an International Baccalaureate (IB) World School with an MYP (Middle Year Program) that focuses on the ARTS. NPA scholars are nurtured to become exemplary citizens and lifelong learners through our mission of developing internationally minded individuals with inquiring and creative minds, a sense of understanding and compassion for others, and the courage to walk their PATH (Perseverance, Accountability, Thoughtfulness, Honesty). As a neighborhood community school we aspire to provide a supportive environment where all students can achieve a passion for excellence and a love for the arts. We have grown into a beacon of intellectual distinction and a place where children are provided with the tools to flourish as lifelong learners who embody the ten IB Learner Profile Attributes. We are an authorized AVID (Advanced Via Individual Determination) school that focuses on college and career strategies that builds up the core of our instruction. Our main community partners include: DreamYard Project, Salvadori Center, MonteFiore Health Center (Full On-Site Health Clinic), Astor (On-Site Mental Health Clinic), LEAP (After-School Enrichment Program), Release the Grip (Community Safety Partnership), and Center for Supportive Schools (Our Key Community Partner).
