overview: One World Middle School is a small school committed to understanding 'who' the child is in order to teach them. Our school is modeled after the United Nations and when children enter, they are referred to as Ambassadors-in-Training until they become ambassadors. Our multifaceted curriculum includes High School Regents courses, Civic Engagement, Music, Orchestra, Band, STEM, Farming, Art, and Coding. We believe a well-rounded education is the key to success. We see Broadway shows, take part in Acts of Kindness and ensure our ambassadors have opportunities to travel overnight. We have visited Historically Black Colleges, Harvard, Yale, Northeastern, SUNY schools, Georgetown to name a few. We have explored the Rocky Mountains to Niagara Falls. In the past 5 years, ambassadors have walked the path of great Civil Rights activists by visiting places such as Selma, Martin Luther King's childhood home, Little Rock Nine and the Lorraine Hotel. We are proud to be an ASD NEST where our staff is dedicated to understanding the needs of all children and developing relationships to ensure success. Teachers will stay late, proctor study hall or bring children up for lunch to help them. Highlights include Orchestra, Basketball, Track, Flag Football, Broadway Jr., Dancing, Art, Spoken Word.We have partnerships with Google, Education through Music, DREAM and Mouse. We also earned the honor of being named a Respect for All School for the past 4 years.

overview: At Park Slope Collegiate, we are committed to creating and maintaining a diverse and integrated student body and faculty. We believe that students learn best in a heterogeneous environment where they can compare what they know and think with the knowledge and ideas of adult scholars as well as with the knowledge and ideas of their classmates. Our very small middle school offers students the opportunity to grow and learn with classmates from diverse backgrounds within an engaging setting. Teachers accustomed to heterogeneous classrooms provide students a variety of individual and group learning experiences. Once a week, students meet in circles to strengthen the community of the classroom by learning more about each other, practicing active listening skills, playing group games, and exploring their social and emotional interests. As a 6-12 school, we also guarantee a seat in our high school for any middle school student interested in continuing at Park Slope Collegiate. Park Slope Collegiate is dedicated to NY States classroom reduction plan and has taken steps to maintain class sizes under 21 students in each of its 6th and 7th grade classes the last two years. The plan is to continue the reduced class sizes moving forward. overview: Being a member of our school community means being part of a vibrant, intellectually curious, and culturally rich environment. In grades 6-8, students engage in the International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (MYP), learning to think critically and make real-world connections across subjects. Our instructional approach is built around inquiry, reflection, and student voice, showcased through Socratic Seminars as well as Declamation, a tradition where students perform speeches and poetry. In 8th grade, complete their Service as Action MYP Project and enter the Associate Degree Discovery Programme (ADDP), which introduces them to college-level expectations. Our mantra, "7 years, 1 school, 1 family," reflects our Early College model with students remaining through grade 12 and graduating with an Associate Degree. As a Performing Arts school, we offer courses in theater, dance, music, and visual arts, where students express themselves through performance, choreography, sculpture, painting, and creative design. Our House System (Yale, UTech, Howard, Columbia) builds identity, leadership, and supports our Restorative Justice program. overview: Our PS/MS 278 community is dedicated to the success of all students. While we offer a rigorous academic curriculum culminating in the 8th Grade Algebra Regents, we prioritize a whole-child approach to learning providing an environment where students can thrive academically, socially, emotionally, and physically. Our talented instructors implement the Schoolwide Enrichment Model (SEM), creating dynamic opportunities for student engagement across the arts, sciences, and beyond. Enrichment experiences include visual arts, music, STEM, Career Day, Science and Robotics Fairs, as well as concerts and classroom showcases that celebrate student learning. To ensure academic growth for all, we offer a range of extended learning opportunities, including After School, Holiday Break, and Saturday Academies, as well as a Junior High School Art Portfolio Program to support aspiring artists. We are proud of our vibrant partnerships, which expand what's possible for our students. These include a school-based mental health clinic and prevention team through Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital; 92nd Street Y Music and Dance; after-school sports such as basketball, volleyball, softball, cheerleading, and track & field at the Armory; ICS/Compass free after school and holiday programming; Center for Arts Education; Creative Arts Works; and The Situation Project, which brings middle school students to two Broadway productions each year. Our school day is supported by family-friendly programming including a free early drop-off breakfast program beginning at 7:30 a.m. and after-school programs available Monday through Friday for all grades.

overview: P.S./I.S. 95 is a culturally diverse school in the heart of Gravesend, Brooklyn. Our mission is to provide a safe and nurturing environment where every student is encouraged to be a lifelong learner. All students are exposed to an integrated curriculum which focuses on academics as well as social and emotional needs. As a Leader in Me partnership school, the entire school community strives to develop and support leadership qualities within our students. Students in grades six through eight have the experience of middle school in a smaller environment where all staff knows each individual child. Our free afterschool program in partnership with NIA offers students an opportunity to participate in various teams including basketball, soccer, and volleyball. Additional programs include Model United Nations Debate Team, CASA Arts Mural program, and free test prep offerings for the Specialized High School Assessment Test, Regents Test Prep, and SOAR Academy for State Exam preparation.

overview: The Academy at PS/MS 122 strives to provide all students with an opportunity to meet their maximum potential and be prepared for even the most difficult of academic challenges at the high school level and beyond. The modern world changes rapidly, and a major goal of our school is to prepare students to meet the unknown challenges of tomorrow. To achieve this, the school offers academic courses which focus on key mathematical concepts, critical thinking, and written and verbal communication skills. Our aim is to provide a foundation of skills that will serve students well in high school, in the workplace, and beyond. Students enrolled in accelerated courses will graduate withhigh school credit in Algebra I, Living Environment, U.S. History and Spanish. The Academy provides a large menu of elective club classes to further student proficiency in areas of interest. Examples of clubs are the guitar club, hydroponic club, movie club, Latin dance club, robotics club, the chess club and a student council. PS/MS 122 believes that it is imperative to support our students' social emotional learning. All students at the Academy will be enrolled in an Advisory section to support their academic and social development during the critical middle school years. Finally, our school fosters a strong community among the students through the student council, college trips, student fundraisers, and school dances.

overview: Welcome to PS/MS 149 Sojourner Truth, respectfully known as Sotru, where Leaders are Created to Change the World. We are devoted to making an impactful change in the lives of students and their families. Our instruction goes beyond the classroom, preparing students for a successful future by building on everyday experiences. In addition to our strong academic framework, students are exposed to geographic areas outside of New York City through annual trips to Washington D.C. and upstate New York, where they learn to ski and snowboard. To ensure student success, we have partnered with the Harlem Children's Zone (HCZ) after-school program. HCZ offers a variety of activities, including dance, science fairs, skateboarding, lacrosse, and a year-round basketball camp. We also believe in the importance of social emotional health. Through our partnership with the New York Foundling Mental Health Clinic, we offer daily services right in the school building to support the mental health of our community. As a community school, we provide additional support to families with a school store, a care closet, and a laundry room, as well as school supplies and uniforms for students. With the support of our community and staff, our vision of creating future leaders is possible.

overview: At PS/IS 173, we are dedicated to creating a vibrant community where all students engage in high-level, rigorous academic learning. We hold high expectations for our diverse student body and leverage the unique strengths of our staff to meet the needs of every learner. Our K-3rd grade classes utilize a phonics program grounded in the Science of Reading research, ensuring a solid foundation in literacy. For our K-8th grade English Language Arts curriculum, we implement the knowledge-building approach of Expeditionary Learning, while our math instruction is guided by the problem-based curriculum, Illustrative Math. Our instructional practices align with the key priorities of our District and NYC, specifically NYC Reads and NYC Solves, to create cohesive learning experiences across all classrooms. We believe in educating the whole child, employing a social-emotional approach that emphasizes recognizing emotions and developing healthy strategies for emotional regulation and expression.In grades 4-8, students have the opportunity to participate in various sports, including boys' and girls' basketball, soccer, a boys' baseball team, and a girls' volleyball team. We also partner with Studio in a School to enhance our visual arts program, ensuring that all students have access to creative opportunities. Throughout the year, students engage in dance, music, and writing residencies with organizations such as Behind the Book and the Dance Project of Washington Heights. Additionally, our Middle School students participate in a study with Weill Cornell Medical at NY Presbyterian, exploring various STEM careers. We are also proud to offer a School-Based Mental Health Clinic. We aim to create a nurturing environment that fosters academic success and personal growth for all students.

Proudly ranked #17 for Standout Middle Schools and #29 for Best Public K-8 Schools across all of New York State. As a pioneer in bilingual education, PS 184M offers a comprehensive Chinese-English Dual Language program alongside Integrated Co-Teaching (ICT) classrooms from K-8, ensuring an inclusive, high-achieving environment for all learners. Backed by an exceptional 96-99% daily attendance rate, our dedicated educators nurture fluent, bicultural student leaders prepared for elite high school placements. We fully support working families with an array of daily After School Program options (Mon - Fri, 2:40 - 5:00 p.m.) focused on enrichment and homework support. At Shuang Wen, we bridge cultures, inspire lifelong learning, and ensure every student succeeds

overview: At P.S./I.S. 184, our motto is: "Where Excellence Is Expected and Greatness Is Created." We uphold and implement our motto on a daily basis with the entire school community. Our goal is to create a community school where parents, staff, students, and the community are collectively responsible for developing the future leaders of our community and world. Our mission is to raise student achievement, improve instructional practices, and optimize school progress by providing all members of the school community with the necessary professional learning to create effective change. As a Community Learning School, we have access to a wide array of additional resources to support the entire community.

overview:
At Public School 189 - The Bilingual Center, we are dedicated to fostering academic excellence by offering students a well-rounded educational experience. Our diverse student body has the opportunity to learn a foreign language, choosing between French or Spanish. We provide six Regents courses: Algebra 1, English, Living Environment, Earth Science, and World Languages for both French and Spanish. Our curriculum is enriched with a robust performing arts program, featuring drama, band, dance, vocal music, and visual arts.
To further support our students' growth, we offer an extensive afterschool program, partnering with organizations like the Brooklyn Children s Museum (Grades K-5), Brooklyn Community Services (Grades 6-8), and Cub Scouts (Grades K-5). Our partnerships with the Metropolitan Museum, Kings County Mental Health, and the Brooklyn Children s Museum enhance studentseducational experiences both in and outside the classroom.
Additionally, we offer financial literacy education, ensuring students develop essential life skills. Throughout the school year, students have the opportunity to attend cultural and educational events, including visits to the Museum of Moving Image and other performing arts performances, broadening their understanding of the world and encouraging creativity.

overview: P.S./I.S. 192, The Magnet School for Math and Science Inquiry, is a PreK - 8 school. We are a small, diverse community focused on academic excellence and social emotional growth. Our Middle School offers an atmosphere where each scholar is known and celebrated. Our school offers many accelerated learning opportunities to explore topics such as STEAM, Visual Arts, Spanish, Music and Career Readiness. Our school offers an honors math class for incoming 6th graders as well as the Algebra I and Biology Regents in 8th grade. We have an array of electives, including sports, chess, acting, science and math olympiads, canvas painting, the green team (student environmental activists), etc. Our talented, dedicated teachers use data to drive instruction and create lessons using scaffolds and supports to meet the needs of all scholars. Our school offers all needed supports for SWD's and ENL scholars. P.S./I.S. 192 offers the NIA afterschool program for all 6th-8th graders. During this program your child will receive homework assistance and extracurricular activities curated to students interests, including but not limited to: Sports, Cooking, Graphic Designs and Step Class. NIA also offers numerous trips throughout the year. We also have after school band and drama club programs.

overview: The Academy of Innovative Science is scheduled to open at IS 206 in September of 2026. Through project-based learning students develop content knowledge and real-world skills in engaging ways. Curiosity drives learning and critical thinking is built through a collaborative, student-centered approach. Digital literacy is cultivated through AI projects that teach students to ask questions and shape a future where technology is used fairly and wisely. Students can also apply their newfound skills in one of our many clubs including Debate Team, Student Volunteers, Gardening Crew, Journalism Club,  or at our annual school play. Our school is home to students from all around the world and we believe multilingualism is a strength to be nurtured. We are proud to offer both Spanish and Russian as world languages. Additionally, our 8th grade students participate in rigorous curricula including Algebra and New Visions Biology. IS 206 endorses and nourishes a community where students, teachers, staff, parents, administrators, and community leaders are dedicated to academic excellence, mutual respect, and equality for all.

overview: We are proud of our school. Teachers, students, and families are dedicated. We practice the concept of social justice, which we translate to mean Equity Access, maximum inclusion for all. Parents appreciate how our school provides a challenging curriculum within a small learning community that promotes positive behavior. Our collaborative teams work together to set goals, plan for effective instruction, and monitor and assess student performance. The skills and strategies that students gain enable them to attain success and reach their potential. Our skilled staff supports families in many ways. overview: PS/IS 66 is a vibrant 3K-8 community school where excellence, innovation, and opportunity come together to empower every learner. Located in the heart of Canarsie, Brooklyn, we are committed to ensuring that all students are academically challenged, socially supported, and prepared to thrive in an ever-changing world. At PS/IS 66, we foster a culture built on our core values of Trust, Loyalty, and Children First, creating an environment where every child is seen, heard, valued, and inspired to reach their fullest potential. Through rigorous, standards-based instruction, students engage in meaningful learning experiences that promote critical thinking, collaboration, creativity, and problem-solving. Our students benefit from a diverse range of enrichment opportunities, including Culinary Arts, Dance, Violin, Music Therapy, Martial Arts, Chess, Debate, Step, Podcasting, Gardening, Student Council, and the National Junior Honor Society. Through initiatives such as Career and Financial Literacy Fridays, community partnerships, and leadership opportunities, students develop the skills and confidence needed for future success. We proudly implement NYC Reads through Wit & Wisdom and NYC Solves through i-Ready Classroom Mathematics, ensuring all students receive high-quality, research-based instruction. Beyond academics, we prioritize social-emotional wellness through restorative practices, peer leadership opportunities, mindfulness supports, and a strong sense of belonging. At PS/IS 66, families, staff, and community partners work together as one village to cultivate responsible, resilient, and compassionate leaders. As Canarsie Blue Jays, we believe that excellence is not simply an expectation, it is our standard.

overview:
PS/IS 87 Middle Village is a zoned 3K - Grade 8 school. We are dedicated to developing future leaders, encouraging students to become advocates for humanity, and fostering an appreciation for diversity, culture, and individual differences. Students learn in a safe, nurturing environment guided by the school mantra: "Treat people the way they want to be treated." We celebrate the diversity of our community through celebrations that honor cultures, holidays, and traditions within our school. These experiences help students develop respect, empathy, and a deeper understanding of the world around them. We offer an Honors Program with a rigorous Regents track. The program promotes academic excellence and prepares students for success in high school and beyond. Mandarin is our language program, providing students with the opportunity to develop language skills while gaining an appreciation for Chinese culture. The school also encourages
teamwork, leadership, and healthy competition through the CHAMPS program and a variety of athletic teams, including track, basketball, and volleyball.
Students are encouraged to participate in extracurricular activities that build
confidence, sportsmanship, and school pride. Our Broadway Junior Program has
developed a growing theater program that allows students to explore the
performing arts, build confidence, and develop skills in acting, singing and
stage production while showcasing their talents. PS/IS 87 values strong community partnerships and collaborates with organizations such as the Greater Ridgewood Youth Council, NYC Swim for Life and NYC Parks Department. These partnerships enrich student learning and provide meaningful opportunities for leadership development, community service, environmental awareness, and educational growth.

overview: Are you ready for an exciting middle school journey? At The Benjamin Franklin Health and Science Academy (PS/IS 157), we offer a unique and vibrant learning experience designed to foster critical thinking and prepare students for leadership. Why Choose Us? Our students engage in hands-on learning through our Native Garden: Learn about local plants and ecosystems. Makerspace: Participate in creative projects using state-of-the-art tools and technology. Chicken Coop: A unique opportunity to experience sustainable living. Kitchen Classroom: Learn the joys of cooking and nutrition. We offer a variety of high-interest clubs and a yoga and meditation room for mindfulness. Our 8th graders have the opportunity to take the NYS Math Regents exam, and we use restorative practices to support our students' emotional and social well-being. Our school reflects the rich diversity of New York City, with approximately 400 students from 3K through 8th grade. We take pride in our inclusive environment, which includes 38% English Language Learners and 17% students with disabilities. We are committed to partnering with students, caregivers, and the community to provide a dynamic and engaging educational experience. We emphasize rigorous academic support, emotional nurturing, and social engagement to ensure holistic development. We maintain strong home-school connections through monthly meetings, workshops, and bilingual communication. The Benjamin Franklin Health and Science Academy is more than just a school; it is a community dedicated to the growth of every student. We invite you to join our school family!

overview: PS/IS 266Q is a non-zoned Pre K-8 District 26 school located on the beautiful Frank Padavan Campus in Bellerose, Queens. We are dedicated to #highstandards & #academicexcellence, while cultivating a nurturing environment supporting children's social-emotional development. PS/IS 266Q empowers students in the classroom to take ownership of learning opportunities. Students are immersed in inquiry-based learning across all subject areas, challenging them to engage in close reading and produce writing and work products that showcase their content knowledge and voice as a writer. PS/IS 266Q has embraced the Citywide Literacy initiative and emerged as a Phase 1 school for the integration of the HMH ELA curriculum. Additionally, our Amplify Science curriculum is lab oriented and combines hands-on and technology-driven lessons that maximize students' learning opportunities. Our approach to math instruction includes a balance of authentic, real-world tasks, established speaking and listening protocols for engaging math-talk and hands-on differentiated work. Our schoolwide transition to adopting the Illustrative Math curriculum during school year 25-26 supported our ability to further our schoolwide proficiency with mathematics. By the Eighth grade, all students are prepared for access to the Algebra I and/or Biology Regents Examinations. With our focus on positive supports for the whole child, we also believe strongly in the learning that occurs outside of academics. We offer activities such as a Pre-K-8 Drama program and award-winning Festival Choir, student leadership opportunities at the Elementary and Middle School levels through our Student Union and PRIDE of 266Q Newspaper Team, athletic clubs and teams, such as well as basketball and volleyball through CHAMPS and D26.

overview: PS/IS 295Q provides opportunities for students to Achieve their Educational Excellence, become Responsible and Respectful Citizens; to embrace lifelong Learning in a Safe and Positive Environment through Teamwork within the school community. At PS/IS 295Q, all students are expected to maintain an average of 65% or above in all classes. For our screened middle school program students are on track to take the Regents Exams in Algebra I, Living Environment, Second Language Proficiency and expected to maintain an average of 85% or above. It is a shared responsibility between the school and parents to provide students with appropriate support when they exhibit difficulty in achieving these expectations. PSIS 295Q is a member of the National Junior Honor Society. The objectives of the PSIS 295Q Chapter of the National Junior Honor Society are as follows: create an enthusiasm for superior scholarship; develop citizenship; stimulate a desire to serve; promote leadership; instill in our youth exemplary qualities of character. Middle school students placed in the National Junior Honor Society must maintain an average of 90% in all subject areas to be considered for the highest award. This includes Visual Arts, Music, Foreign Language, Technology, Library, and Physical Education to be considered for the highest award.

overview: Welcome to PS/IS 30 Mary White Ovington, a vibrant K-8 school nestled in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn. Known for our commitment to diversity and nurturing environment, we are dedicated to meeting the needs of every student. Our dynamic staff ensures academic excellence across all subjects, fostering growth and achievement. Guided by our ROAR principles of Respect, Opportunity, Acceptance, and Resilience, we create a supportive community where every child can flourish.PS/IS 30 proudly hosts NYC's only dual language Arabic immersion program, in grades K-8, enriching our students' linguistic and cultural education. Additionally, all K-8 students have the opportunity to explore the arts through electives in visual arts, dance, music, and theatre. Affiliated with Broadway Bound Junior, we stage annual musicals that showcase our students' talents. We have a growing Band and Orchestra program. Exciting developments are underway at PS/IS 30, including the transformation of our library into a state-of-the-art media center featuring a computer room and podcast studio. Our partnership with NIA, a community-based organization, enhances our students' experience by offering seamless access to extracurricular activities in science, math, the arts, and sports.As a Leader in Me school, we empower our students to take ownership of their learning journey and develop leadership skills from an early age. Join us as we inspire and prepare our students to excel in academics, creativity, and leadership.

overview: Students at PS/IS 384 often say that the school feels like a part of their family. As a 3K - 8th grade school, many students have spent nine years or more in our building, and have truly become part of our family. Our school is a place where all students are held to high expectations, and are pushed to be the best they can be. Our students understand that hard work always pays off, and we ensure that all students are challenged. We have a Dual Language program so that students can become fluent in both Spanish and English.We are a "Kids at Hope" school, a place in which all teachers, staff and community members believe that all children can achieve success, no exceptions. In a caring, warm school environment, our students are comfortable taking risks. Our students go on many wonderful trips around NYC to visit the Statue of Liberty, attend a Major League Baseball game, or take a walking tour of Chinatown. Many of our classrooms are filled with interesting class pets so our students can learn about caring for animals. At PS/IS 384 we want our parents to feel supported, so the school has an open door policy, and parents are welcome to come in and speak with the principal or teachers at any time.

overview: PSMS 31 is a K-8 school that offers a comprehensive educational experience focusing on both academic learning and social-emotional development. The school serves students in 3K, 4K, and K-8 grades. PSMS 31 follows a holistic approach to education, aiming to nurture well-rounded individuals who are prepared to succeed in both academics and interpersonal skills.Aligned with District 7's vision of being the bridge to generational success, PSMS 31 is committed to providing innovative and transformational opportunities to its students. The school offers accelerated courses in subjects such as Algebra, Living Environment, and US History Regents, allowing students to excel academically.In addition to traditional academic subjects, PSMS 31 provides a variety of extracurricular programs to enrich the students' educational experience. These programs include the Broadway Jr Theater program, financial literacy, West African drums and dance, modern dance, band, debate club, My Brother and Sisters Keeper, hydroponics, coding, and virtual reality.Furthermore, PSMS 31 collaborates with community-based organizations to offer additional activities such as cooking, painting, dance, basketball, volleyball, and step. The school believes that every lesson is an experience and strives to provide a learning environment that empowers students to become active and engaged citizens who can excel and lead in their communities and beyond.Overall, PSMS 31 aims to provide a well-rounded education that prepares students not only for academic success but also for personal growth and leadership roles in their communities.

overview: Our middle school offers a rich and engaging experience that supports both academic excellence and student development. Students participate in the arts through Broadway Jr., chorus, dance/step, and visual art. We are committed to fostering a positive and supportive school culture through schoolwide restorative practices and peer mediation, as well as through student-led podcasts and daily school news broadcasts. As a Community School, we bring students, families, and staff together through events such as community dinners that build meaningful connections. Students in grades 7 and 8 engage in College Access for All, including visits to college campuses, helping them envision their futures beyond middle school. Leadership and engagement are encouraged through opportunities like Student Government. We offer a wide range of academic supports and enrichment opportunities, including our Rise and Thrive club program, Elevate after school program, and Saturday Academy to prepare for New York State exams build strong foundational math and literacy skills. Our school provides extensive after-school programming for all K-8 students through a partnership with NYJTL, ensuring that every student has access to enrichment, sports, and academic support.

overview: We are delighted that you are entrusting your child to our care. At The Van Nest Academy, we strive to be a safe, nurturing, and inviting community for you and your family. We hope to create a lasting partnership with you until your child is ready to advance to high school and beyond. At the core of our philosophy is the pursuit of academic excellence and the belief that every child can and must succeed. Our goal is to create a joyful, lifelong learner who is confident, caring, and knowledgeable. We provide an outstanding academic program, an inclusive environment, and a unique experience collaborating with local medical and environmental education facilities. Students will work with real-world scientists, both in the classroom and in their workplaces, to become creative problem-solvers and responsible citizens. In addition to our rigorous curriculum in Literacy, Mathematics, Science, and Social Studies, students participate in an interactive music program, the ART of observation, and regular physical education and health instruction. We also fully integrate technology into the classroom as a tool for all students to access information, solve problems, and share knowledge. To solidify our sense of community, we invite you to take an active role as our learning partners and to share your interests and talents with us.

overview:
The Ronald McNair School is committed to providing a rigorous and nurturing learning environment where all students are empowered to achieve academic excellence, think critically, and develop the skills needed for lifelong success. 
The Ronald McNair School offers a comprehensive, standards-based curriculum designed to meet the diverse needs of all learners. Instruction focuses on: 
English Language Arts, Mathematics, Science, and Social Studies 
Integration of technology to enhance learning 
Differentiated instruction to support varied learning styles 
Enrichment and intervention programs to ensure student growth 
The school is supported by a dedicated team of educators and staff who are committed to fostering a culture of high expectations, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
The Ronald McNair School serves a diverse student population and promotes an inclusive environment where respect, responsibility, and resilience are central values. Students are encouraged to take ownership of their learning and contribute positively to the school community. 
Students have access to a variety of enrichment activities, which may include: 
Academic clubs and leadership opportunities 
Arts and music programs 
Physical education and athletics 
STEM-related activities and hands-on learning experiences 
The school values strong partnerships with families and the local community to support student success. Engagement opportunities include: 
Parent workshops and school events 
Open communication between staff and families 
Community partnerships that enhance student learning 
The Ronald McNair School is dedicated to continuous improvement, focusing on student achievement, equity, and preparing all learners for future academic and career success.

overview: At PS/MS 200, The Magnet School of Global Studies & Leadership, our mission is to help students realize their potential as leaders in the classroom, school, neighborhood, nation, and world. We foster an environment that gives students, staff, and families a voice. We instill in students the understanding that we only learn when we are being challenged to think deeply. We cultivate the belief that we can always improve, even if we are struggling. We recognize the far-reaching impact of compassion for others and we celebrate diversity and its many benefits to our school community.We are a small school, but we span Grades 3K - 8. At our school, there is a 1:13 teacher-to-student ratio, which enables students and staff members to build strong relationships. Due to our small size and low teacher-to-student ratio, the school community is characterized by a true family spirit. Students in Grades 6-8 study global issues and consider ways in which they can make a difference at a young age. In addition to core subjects, our middle school students can learn about theater, visual arts, spanish, coding, and more. We have a student government and a student-run school newspaper. Students are invited to exercise at school before the first period of the day and we have a free after-school program.

overview: Our bold & unapologetic vision is that EVERY QUMS student will meet and exceed New York State standards in all subjects. We are successfully building a safe and nurturing learning community through the committed partnership of like-minded families, PTA leadership, faculty & staff, and community supporters. QUMS offers extensive academic support through strong classroom instruction, targeted tutoring opportunities, and social-emotional support for all students from our dynamic guidance and social work team. QUMS offers an after-school SHSAT program for qualified students in 6th and 7th grades to prepare to sit for the SHSAT in the fall of their 8th grade year. This program has resulted in our students receiving acceptances into Stuyvesant High School, Brooklyn Technical High School, Queens High School for the Sciences at York College, and The Brooklyn Latin School. Additional early high school opportunities at QUMS include offering Regents courses in Life Sciences: Biology, Algebra 1, and U. S. History and Government based on equity. QUMS also offers a variety of activities such as Student Council, Robotics, Cooking Club, Chess Club, Language Club, Media Club, Photography Club, Soccer Club, and SONYC-- our free after school program. SONYC provides students with a broad range of cross-curricular and extracurricular experiences including sports, dance & arts, and STEM exploration.

overview: At Quest middle school, learning is an adventure grounded in game-like learning, social-emotional learning, and the development of 21st-century skills. We believe that game-like learning is a powerful vehicle for delivering rigorous, standards-based instruction, engaging students in meaningful challenges that spark curiosity, creativity, and deep academic thinking. Through immersive, project-based experiences, students collaborate to solve authentic problems, build academic mastery, and develop critical skills such as communication, collaboration, creativity, and problem-solving. Teachers design engaging learning experiences that make complex content accessible and challenging while maintaining high expectations for all learners. Students demonstrate their learning through collaborative projects, authentic performance tasks, and design challenges that connect classroom learning to real-world applications. Small class sizes and Home Base advisory routines ensure every student is known, supported, and challenged. We build community, promote social-emotional learning, and support academic growth, helping students develop resilience, self-awareness, and a strong sense of belonging. We provide all students with rigorous learning opportunities, including Earth and Space Science and Algebra I Regents courses in eighth grade that offer the opportunity to earn high school credit and Regents exams.

Students are strongly encouraged to sign up for our after-school program which runs from 3:10pm-6pm. During this time, students engage in both academic work and enrichment clubs. overview: Scholars’ Academy is a top-ranked, highly rigorous school recognized by U.S. News & World Report across New York City, New York State, and the nation. At the heart of our success is a dedicated team of educators and staff who prioritize strong, meaningful connections with students and families ensuring every student thrives academically, socially, and emotionally. Our robust learning programs foster positive peer relationships, promote cultural understanding, elevate student voice, and support overall well-being. In the classroom, Scholars engage in an inquiry-based, hands-on learning environment where collaboration and rich, student-driven discussions deepen understanding and critical thinking. Teachers at Scholars’ Academy design engaging, standards-based instruction enhanced by a variety of innovative digital tools. This dynamic approach ensures that learning remains both rigorous and relevant. Students at Scholars’ Academy also have the unique opportunity to accelerate their academic journey. By the end of eighth grade, all students complete three high school Regents courses: Algebra, Biology, and Spanish earning valuable high school credits. In addition, students explore their passions by selecting elective courses aligned to their individual interests and talents, meeting twice weekly to enrich their overall experience.

overview: The School for Global Leaders is a 6-12 International Baccalaureate World School offering an authorized IB Middle Years Programme (MYP). Families love our small class sizes, dynamic teaching team, and warm classroom environments. We make learning relevant by encouraging collaborative work and problem solving as students explore community and world issues. All eighth-grade students complete a community project that encourages them to implement service as action. Alongside a challenging and engaging IB Curriculum, we offer a robust Arts and elective program. Students select at least one elective per year from options like: Instrumental music, Culinary, Gardening and Ecology, Weight Training, Dance, and Theatre. We also offer an Advanced Visual Arts course and Integrated Algebra. Global Leaders is more than just a school; we are a family who learns, plays, grows, and supports one another. Note: We are also a Candidate School for the Diploma and Career-related IB Programmes, actively pursuing authorization. These are schools that share a common philosophy and commitment to high quality, challenging, international education that we believe is important for our students. For further information about the IB and its programmes, visit www.ibo.org

overview: At School of the Future Brooklyn, students are challenged, supported, and inspired to become the leaders, innovators, and problem-solvers of tomorrow. As a college-preparatory middle school, we provide a rigorous academic program in a nurturing environment where every scholar is known, valued, and encouraged to reach their fullest potential. Our STEAM-focused curriculum integrates science, technology, engineering, the arts, and mathematics through hands-on, real-world learning experiences that spark curiosity and creativity. Students explore concepts through innovative programs such as our immersive ZSpace laboratories, where biology and other sciences come to life through interactive 3D technology. At SOFBK, learning extends beyond the classroom. Scholars participate in college visits, educational day trips, career exploration experiences, and community-based projects that broaden their perspectives and help them envision their future success. Our culturally responsive curriculum reflects the diverse identities, histories, and experiences of our students, fostering a strong sense of belonging and pride. We emphasize literacy and communication across all subject areas, teaching students to think critically, articulate their ideas with confidence, use academic vocabulary, and support their thinking with evidence. Through high expectations, personalized support, and meaningful learning experiences, we prepare students to excel in high school, college, careers, and as engaged citizens in an ever-changing world.

overview: We are a community that THINKS! 100 students per grade & 25-28 students to a class. Teachers meet weekly to discuss students' progress and follow up with parents regarding concerns. Students meet in circles of 10-12 students weekly to discuss community issues, current events, decision making, healthy relationships, coping skills, etc. Our focus is on character and emotional development as well as strong academics. We are a small school with big opportunities. Drama, Art, Music and Computer Science are offered for electives - Students rotate through all electives in 6th and 7th grade, and choose electives 8th. Foreign language is Spanish and Mandarin starting in 7th grade. FREE Afterschool Program Sports (girls and boys basketball, flag football, volleyball, soccer baseball, softball, track and more!) School musical + Middle School Play International trip opportunities. We are a 6-12 school. The vast majority of our middle school students stay on through high school. 100% of our graduating seniors are accepted to college, many with scholarships. SOF graduates can be found in such illustrious schools as Yale, Cornell, Smith College, Wesleyan, Columbia, University of Virginia, Carnegie Mellon, SUNY Binghamton, Hampshire, NYU, Hunter, and Skidmore.

overview: Mott Hall Science and Technology Academy is a rigorous, math, science, and technology-focused middle school that offers families an opportunity for their children to meet the highest academic expectations and standards. Our mission is to cultivate international mindedness, encourage students to think beyond the boundaries of their community, and prepare them for smooth transitions to selective high schools and competitive admission to top public and private colleges. We are proud to be the first stand-alone International Baccalaureate (IB) certified public middle school in New York City. Our IB program empowers students to become critical thinkers, compassionate leaders, and globally minded citizens. Through inquiry-based learning, interdisciplinary projects, and a focus on real-world connections, students develop strong academic and personal skills that prepare them for success in high school and beyond. We are also an AVID-certified school. AVID (Advancement Via Individual Determination) equips our students with essential academic and organizational skills, fosters a college-going mindset, and provides structured support to help them succeed in rigorous coursework. Through AVID, students develop strong writing, inquiry, collaboration, and reading strategies, while also building confidence and leadership skills. In addition to our academic excellence, we offer a strong theater curriculum that nurtures creativity, confidence, and collaboration. Our students have performed in acclaimed productions such as Mean Girls, High School Musical, and Once on This Island. Our school culture is shaped by a shared vision for academic excellence, personal growth, and the belief that all students can and will succeed in their endeavors, whether in STEM, the arts, or beyond.

Students specialize in one of three vibrant arts pathways, media arts, theater, or dance, while developing their linguistic and emotional intelligence through our English as a New Language (ENL), Spanish Dual Language, and mentorship programs. Families value our dedicated educators who design instruction that connects student interests to real-world applications. overview: The mission of the Special Music School is to teach musically gifted children through highly structured instrumental training and a standards-based academic program. The school prepares students for professional music careers while recognizing that not every student will choose such a career. The underlying philosophy of the Special Music School is the belief that music education for gifted pupils requires: 1) extensive opportunities to work one-to-one with an outstanding instrumental faculty; 2) a structured, sequential music curriculum; 3) opportunities to perform before audiences; and 4) interaction between general academics and musical studies. Our goal is to see each child reach his or her academic and musical potential. Our vision is that all students will become lifelong learners and critical thinkers in our caring and respectful learning environment. We encourage parental involvement in all aspects of the school.

overview: Dr. Sun Yat Sen Middle School believes that there is genius in every child. By providing many venues for our students to develop as scholars and people, ranging from our core curriculum in which all of our 8th graders take a number of regents classes, and experience a curriculum full of reading, writing and discussion, there is something to challenge every student. Our intensive arts programs prepare students to apply for arts focused high schools in their choice of dance, music, digital art or visual art.Through their trips to the both near and far (8th graders take a two night trip to Washington, D.C.), they learn to expand their horizons beyond the city limits. In addition to pushing our students academically, we teach our children positive social and emotional skills. Our advisory programs uses the principles of restorative practices to help students learn from their mistakes rather than just be punished by them. Our Student Government and GSA provide ways for students to take leadership in our school. Our faculty and staff work hard to build connections, which shows with the number of our alumni who come back to visit throughout the year. Please sign up for a group or personal tour so we can show you the great things MS 131 has to offer. Whether you are interested in our Dual Language Mandarin program, our Accelerated Academic Program, ICT or our Horizon program, we would love to meet you!

overview: The Teachers College Community School (TCCS) established in 2011, is a university assisted, non-selective Pre-K-8 demonstration school that applies state of-the-art knowledge and best practices in teaching, learning, and child development. The mission of TCCS is to provide a child-centered environment that will inspire and challenge all of our students to become independent thinkers, problem solvers and life-long learners, and to work as a collaborative unit of parents, faculty and staff to ensure that our students perform their optimal best. We are a nurturing community that believes students learn best through positive framing, setting personalized goals and knowing what they need to do to achieve them. TCCS takes pride in a rigorous curriculum that develops knowledge, concepts, and skills, and encourages proactive and engaged learning. All of our 8th grade students have the opportunity to take the Living Environment, Algebra I and ELA Regent Exams. This allows them to advance to High School with up to three of the five required exams necessary to earn a diploma in NY State. We have a long-standing relationship with Teachers College (TC), Columbia University, which provides expertise and services to ensure student success, including rigorous professional development for teachers and intervention supports for students. Other special features of the school include: customized NGS aligned Math and Science curriculum designed with support from TC, small group targeted interventions and accelerated enrichment, Studio in a School for fine arts, Young Eisner Scholars (YES) partnership, and instrumental, vocal and music composition, and partnership with the NY Phil Harmonic.

overview:
Our school offers an exceptional learning environment where every student can thrive. At PS 347, our relatively small class sizes set us apart from other public schools, allowing each student to receive personalized attention and truly shine. We are a diverse and inclusive community of learners. From Pre-K through 5th grade, our students include CODAs (Children of Deaf Adults), hearing students, Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing children, those connected to the Deaf community, and allies. In middle school, many students are CODAs, while others are eager to learn and explore American Sign Language (ASL). We warmly welcome everyone.
Our mission is to provide a joyful learning environment that balances academic rigor with a strong focus on ASL. Our teachers deliver a District 2 aligned curriculum designed to help all students reach their personal best while building curiosity, empathy, and social awareness through higher-level thinking and real-world learning. We support engagement through programs like middle school basketball before school and a robust after-school program. Our classrooms often include two teachers, ensuring strong support for all learners. We also offer accelerated math, business, Earth Science, and Biology.
Middle school students participate in an 8th-grade trip to Washington, D.C., where they explore Gallaudet University and American history.
Our close-knit community fosters strong family partnerships and supports each child in becoming an independent, responsible, lifelong learner prepared for success.
All signs point to success!

overview:
The John Dewey Annex was founded to expand opportunity,ensuring that all students in our community have access to a coherent, rigorous, and supportive academic pathway beginning in middle school and extending seamlessly through high school graduation. As John Dewey High School evolves into a 6-12 campus, the annex represents a purposeful commitment to early investment in students’ academic identity, skill development, and sense of belonging. Too often, students arrive in high school without the academic habits, confidence, or exposure needed to fully access advanced coursework and specialized programs. The annex addresses this gap by creating a middle school experience that is intentionally aligned with high school expectations, while still honoring the developmental needs of younger learners. At its core, the annex exists to:
Build a strong academic foundation in Grades 6-8
Provide early access to high school-level thinking and opportunities
Ensure equity in preparation for college, careers, and life
Create a smaller, more personalized environment within a large, diverse school community The result is a school model where every student is known, supported, and prepared long before they enter the high-stakes years of high school.

overview: Boerum Hill School for International Studies (BHS) is a diverse, inclusive 6-12 International Baccalaureate (IB) World School located in the heart of Brooklyn. As the only public school in District 15 offering the full IB continuum from grades 6-12, we believe that every child deserves access to a rigorous, engaging, and globally focused education. Our students learn through inquiry, discussion, critical thinking, and real-world problem solving while developing the IB Learner Profile traits of being caring, open-minded, reflective, and principled. BHS offers all students the opportunity to participate in the IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) and pursue the IB Diploma Programme (DP) in high school. Students engage in rich learning experiences including debate, research, interdisciplinary projects, community service, international-mindedness activities, and authentic performance-based assessments. Beyond the classroom, students can participate in athletics, student government, arts programs, clubs, international trips, leadership opportunities, and a wide range of after-school programming. Our school community values strong relationships and personalized support. Through advisory, counseling services, academic intervention programs, and a commitment to inclusive practices, we ensure students are known, challenged, and supported. We are proud of our growing IB Diploma Programme, strong graduation outcomes, improving attendance, and commitment to preparing students for success in college, careers, and life. At BHS, students are encouraged to take intellectual risks, explore their passions, engage with diverse perspectives, and become active contributors to their communities. Our mission is simple: Every Child is Our Child.

overview: A Brooklyn Green School scholar experiences learning as something that extends far beyond the classroom. Our students engage in a rigorous academic program in preparation for high school through challenging coursework, high school-level classes and the opportunity to earn credit by taking the Biology and Algebra Regents exams. Learning is meaningful, relevant, and rooted in real-world experiences. As a project-based learning school, students investigate authentic problems, conduct action research, and apply their learning through field studies, community partnerships, and hands-on experiences. Our eco-activism theme encourages students to become environmental stewards by growing, harvesting, and cooking fresh fruits and vegetables while developing a lifelong commitment to health, wellness, and sustainability. Students discover and develop their passions through a rich arts program that includes visual art, theater, chorus, and band, where they can learn from 10 different instruments. Beyond the school day, a robust after-school program offers additional opportunities in the arts, dance, sports and unique experiences such as boat building and camping. Student voice and leadership are central to the Brooklyn Green experience. Through Student Government, Peer Mediators, the GSA, book clubs, and other student-led organizations, scholars learn to advocate for themselves and others while building confidence and responsibility. Our students also thrive through athletics, participating in track, flag football, competitive cheer, basketball, soccer and volleyball. Brooklyn Green School scholars learn by doing. They graduate as confident, compassionate, and environmentally conscious leaders who are prepared to make a positive impact on their communities and the world.

overview: The Clinton School is a vibrant grades 6 to 12 District 2 community school dedicated to fostering a nurturing, inclusive, and academically rich environment for all students. The primary mission at Clinton is to prepare every young person for the journey ahead, culminating in the prestigious International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme. As an IB Continuum School, Clinton offers a seamless academic pathway consisting of both the Middle Years Programme for grades 6 to 10 and the Diploma Programme for grades 11 and 12. This unique seven-year scope and sequence is intentionally designed to challenge and support a wide range of learners throughout their entire time at the school. From the moment a child enters the sixth grade, acceptance into the full IB pathway is automatic. The school philosophy is built on the belief that every student thrives when given high expectations combined with robust, caring support. The International Baccalaureate framework is a rigorous international program that focuses deeply on the development of the whole child. It requires meaningful learning across six major core content areas, which include Mathematics, Science, English, Social Studies, the Arts, and World Language study in Spanish. Beyond core academics, the curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, international mindedness, and community action, helping students grow into compassionate, globally conscious citizens. Recognizing that middle school is a time of immense growth both inside and outside the classroom, Clinton ensures that learning and engagement continue after the final bell. We have a long-stand partnership with Manhattan Youth, who run our free programs, five days a week.

overview: We are proud to be the first US Department of Education Magnet School in New York City for Career Connected Learning! Our school sets a high academic bar that challenges students to expand their personal and academic visions of themselves. Through partnerships with outside organizations, students learn by connecting with professionals. All of our students take computer science, including block based coding, video game design, and web design.We have a one-to-one Chromebook program, enabling all students to access technology in the classroom and at home. We also offer finance programs where students are immersed in a schoolwide economy with School Bucks, financial courses, school jobs, a school bank, and a school store. The school has been featured in The New York Times, PBS, New York Daily News, Wall Street Journal, NY1 News, and the NY Post for its innovative programs.Class size in the middle school arts program is 15 students, providing for extra creativity and personal attention.All middle school students receive expanded day programming until 5:20 PM Monday through Friday including academic support, arts, and athletics. We have a model Spanish dual language program and most students select our high school program and remain with us for 7 years. Middle school students engage in educational trips and overnight college visits in NYC and beyond including Philadelphia, Boston, and Washington, DC. Finally, we have an amazing sports program including Basketball, Baseball, Soccer, and Lacrosse. overview: Our school community offers students a rigorous and engaging academic program, with a deep commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We understand that the middle school experience is unique, and we offer a safe and fun place to be a kid. Supported by dedicated teaching staff, administration, and PTA, students are provided with opportunities to engage in hands-on, inquiry-based curriculum while constructing knowledge within a meaningful context. Our Exploration Program is an outgrowth of our school's philosophy: middle school students are social individuals and benefit from learning through cooperative groups. The Exploration experience provides students with the opportunity to get off-site and explore city-wide educational institutions. Students have arts (music, theater, dance, visual art, and technology) for all three years. Our advisory program supports students' academic, social, and emotional learning, and we employ restorative practices across our school. Our free after-school program allows students to learn new skills and share common interests, through sports, arts, and leadership. We have earned a Blackboard Award for Outstanding School in Brooklyn and consistent excellent ratings on the School Quality Snapshot.

overview:
Our mission at The Middle School of Media, Law and Fine Arts (MLFA) is to empower our scholars in reaching their highest academic and individual potential through hands-on station-teaching and learning. We strongly believe in Molding Leaders into Fearless Advocates by providing all students with rigorous instruction that exposes them to media, law, and fine arts.
Our renowned academic program includes regents track courses in US History, Living Environment, and Algebra. This is coupled with 5 differentiated intervention classes in literacy and math to expand our scholars' proficiency levels. We offer 6 periods of art/sports electives in various disciplines such as visual arts, drums, horns, media, robotics, contemporary dance, hip hop, track, and varsity basketball. These efforts and offerings have turned into acceptance letters to specialized high schools such as LaGuardia H.S. for the Performing Arts, Brooklyn Technical H.S., and Brooklyn College Academy.
Our scholars can partake in social-emotional skill building morning check-ins, individual/group counseling, meditation services, and high school articulation classes in our state-of-the-art Makerspace, computer lab, and brand new dance studio. This is due to our robust partnerships with at least four Community-Based Organizations that include at least 5 social workers. Students and teachers also enjoy the benefit of utilizing technology in their daily learning as every classroom is equipped with laptops and smartboards. We offer 2 ExpandEd after-school programs that provide an array of extracurricular activities, homework help, and tutoring from 2:40-5:30 pm every day. We hope that after learning about our school, you will join our MLFA family this upcoming year! See you this Fall!

overview: Founded in 1985 as a magnet school for gifted children, the Mott Hall School remains a shining gem in District Six providing an advanced curriculum to our scholars. Our mission is to develop future leaders in Mathematics, Science, and Technology by providing a world-class education that prepares students for high school, college, and higher learning. We provide a rigorous academic curriculum and whole-child program that includes experiences both inside and outside the school building. Mott Hall creates a home away from home atmosphere that inspires students to explore, grow, and ask questions. We provide an advanced curriculum with opportunities to earn high school credits by the end of their eighth grade year. Focusing on restorative practices, we also strive to create an atmosphere that moves our students toward assuming personal and social responsibility. We work closely with community partners, including our treasured partnerships with National Dance Institute, NY Edge, and City College to provide a well-rounded, exciting learning experience for all of our scholars.

overview: You belong at NSLA! We are committed to fostering an inclusive middle school experience, filled with diverse opportunities that ignite creativity and cultivate habits of success. Our rich and engaging curriculum empowers students to be critical thinkers and step into their roles as future leaders. This foundation is elevated by the arts, which are truly at the heart of NSLA. Students immerse themselves in our four dedicated studios: Band, Choir, Dance, and Visual Arts, with even more options after school. Our innovative science program offers hands-on learning in our gardens, connecting students to nature and healthy living. Beyond the classroom, students explore the city, state, and beyond through rewarding trips. We ensure every student receives personalized support from a dedicated School Counselor who guides them and serves as a vital resource for families and teachers throughout their NSLA journey. Knowing how critical family support is, we proudly offer a variety of family workshops, activities, and trips to strengthen our vibrant community bonds. At NSLA, discover your potential and confidently shape your future. This is an extraordinary place to grow, and you truly belong here!

overview: We at RSMA are thrilled to announce that we are in our candidacy to become an accredited International Baccalaureate (IB) school. Our commitment to the IB program, particularly the Middle Years Program (MYP), reflects our dedication to providing a comprehensive and internationally recognized education. The MYP emphasizes intellectual challenge and encourages students to make connections between their studies and the real world. In addition to our core academic classes, we offer a rich array of courses in music, theater, visual arts, design and engineering, and world languages. These offerings reflect our belief in a well-rounded education that nurtures not only the intellect but also the creative spirit of our students. As part of our accelerated math program, all of our students take the Algebra I regents course. We also offer the Biology regents course, ensuring our students receive a solid foundation in the sciences. Beyond the classroom, we provide extensive after-school activities. We offer a free DYCD comprehensive after-school program and an athletics program that includes fall, winter, and spring sports teams. These programs aim to foster teamwork, discipline, and physical fitness among our students. We also provide extensive in-school enrichment activities. These include conservatory-style music and visual arts offerings, hip-hop dance, eSports, digital music creation, videography, and intramural sports. These activities provide our students with opportunities to explore their passions, develop new skills, and express their creativity. At RSMA, we strive to provide an enriching, balanced, and inclusive educational experience for all our students.

overview: The School for Inquiry and Social Justice is a middle school that provides students with opportunities to explore and achieve academic excellence and social advocacy for their community. At MS 337, students engage in academic accelerated course work such as the Algebra (Math) Regents and the Living Environment (Science) Regents. We also provide students with academic intervention opportunities to support growth in reading and math. Our Special Education department ensures that all students across all grades who receive special education services have knowledge of their services and opportunities to participate in making decisions about their needs and how they can best be met. In addition to our afterschool program run by Eastside House, MS 337 has a robust offering of clubs that are taught by teachers. These clubs include Change Agents (focused on community change and service learning), Gender Sexuality Alliance (GSA, focused on inclusivity, Debate, and Music. We also have a strong afterschool sports program including basketball, volleyball, soccer, and cheerleading.We are also fortunate to be a Broadway Junior affiliated school that works alongside production specialists, set designers, teachers, and other support staff all year to produce and perform a Broadway show every spring. This partnership with Broadway Junior has exposed our students to theater experiences that has allowed them to learn acting skills, how to design their own sets, costume making, and managing and working stage lights.MS 337s mission is to educate students with a holistic approach. We believe that is how students learn the value in education.

overview: The School of Integrated Learning M.S. 354 is an International Baccalaureate-IB school, with a focus on college and career readiness. We enrich our scholars with a high quality curriculum, curated to enhance their preparedness for post-secondary education and career. As a newly redesigned STEM+A school, our curriculum emphasizes Science, Technology, Engineering, Math, and the Arts (STEM+A), to challenge scholars to develop problem solving and critical thinking skills. Students engage in exploratory project based learning alongside and be mentored by High school and College students, as we continue to partner with Medgar Evers Preparatory H.S., PTECH, Brooklyn Technical H.S. and NY Institute of Technology. All students engage in Service-Learning Projects as part of the Civics for All Curriculum. Scholars in our Phoenix Academy Screened Program (K354A) are on a track to sit Regents Exams in US History and Government, Integrated Algebra I and Living Environment. All our seventh-grade scholars take the 8th grade NYS Science Test. Students select and participate in one of four academies, Home Economics, Performing Arts, Sports, and Technology, to bolster their Social Emotional Learning and enrich their interests and talents. Most of our scholars are accepted to their first-choice high school, with some attending specialized high schools. All classrooms have SMART Boards; we have a mobile science lab, and laptop carts. As needed, scholars are provided Academic Intervention Services (AIS), to meet the New Generation Learning Standards-NGLS. We use auto-dials, email, text updates, Jupiter, a monthly newsletter, Instagram (@MS354BROOKLYN), and our school website, to keep our parents informed. Families also get the opportunity to see a Broadway show each spring.

overview: The Science and Medicine Middle School 366 is committed to providing a safe and nurturing yet academically rigorous learning environment that prepares students for high school, college, careers, and service to the world. It is our expectation that students respect themselves and others, hold themselves accountable for their actions, and always strive for excellence. We have a medical science teaching lab, complete with hospital-grade beds and equipment. Our students visit various CUNY and SUNY schools to explore careers in health, human services and medical science. Students engage in various hands-on and real-world activities through our partnerships with The Urban Advantage Science Initiative, Weill Cornell Medical College, Elevate Education, InnovationEDU Science, the Scripps National Spelling Bee, the BUILD Entrepreneurship program, the NYCPS Office of Energy and Sustainability, high impact tutoring partner Follow Us to Success, ExpandED and the District 18 Student Advisory Council. We believe that rich and engaging expeditionary learning opportunities are key to students' access to all that our city has to offer. We are partnering with several New York City hospitals and health organizations to bring medical professionals into our classrooms to inspire and encourage our students to pursue careers in health services.

overview: Do you have a child that is struggling to read? Are they a reluctant reader or do they avoid reading altogether? The South Bronx Literacy Academy (SBLA) is the first stand-alone public school in New York City specifically designed to serve students who are struggling to read or have diagnosed dyslexia. SBLA will help your child learn to read by using an instructional approach grounded in the latest research on brain development and the science of reading. Children will participate in daily, explicit, multisensory instruction, along with social emotional support as part of a strong and loving community. SBLA will meet your child where they are and help them reach their academic potential. This school is expanding to serve grade 6 for the 2026-2027 school year, and will serve grades 2 through 8 at scale starting in the 2028-2029 school year.

overview: TMA serves students in grades 6-12 with a mission to prepare them for success in college, careers, and postsecondary training opportunities. As a school community of approximately 400 students, we are able to provide personalized support and build meaningful relationships that help every student thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. Our educational approach emphasizes culturally relevant teaching practices and social-emotional learning, ensuring that students see themselves reflected in their learning experiences while developing the skills needed to succeed in school, work, and life. Through more than twenty community partnerships, students have access to enriching experiences in areas such as technology, design, athletics, and youth development. Our high school students participate in college courses through partnerships with local colleges and universities during their 10th, 11th and 12th grade years, allowing them to earn college credits while still in high school. We also offer mentoring programs that support the growth, leadership, and development of both young women and young men. TMA's athletic offerings include boys' and girls' basketball, track and field, and badminton. For students in grades 6-8, we provide comprehensive wrap-around services through our extended learning time partner, Global Kids Inc. After-school programming runs Monday through Friday from 2:40 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. at no cost to families and includes academic support, enrichment activities, leadership development, and social-emotional learning opportunities that foster confidence, resilience, and community engagement.

overview: Founded in 2001 by a passionate grassroots coalition of families and local educators,Tompkins Square Middle School (TSMS) quickly blossomed into an award-winning NYC public school. We are a joyful, inclusive community with caring expert teachers and a robust integrated advisory program that’s focused specifically on early adolescence. We are also part of the DOE’s class size reduction pilot and our community is thrilled about our new small classes! TSMS was built as a love letter to difference, knowing that our classrooms have always been richer learning spaces for it. Beyond our dynamic core academics, TSMS offers a vibrant school-day Arts for All experience— spanning Music, Visual Art, Theater Arts, and Dance– that we believe is deeply significant for this age group. Over 90% of our 8th graders are matched to one of their top high school choices, and TSMS graduates stay connected to our community. We maintain partnerships with science and arts institutions across the city, and are pleased to have our own rooftop garden and black box theater. At TSMS, we pride ourselves on being a stand-alone middle school: inquisitive children enter our doors and emerge as confident, curious young adults well-prepared for whatever high school they choose.

overview: What makes UNMS truly special is the shared goal of providing a nurturing and enriching school experience for all of our children. We believe that education plays a pivotal role in the academic, emotional, and physical development of every child. Our learning community inspires students because of our dedicated group of educators who foster a passion for learning and a commitment to making a difference. At UNMS, we are committed to working relentlessly to create a learning environment where every child is cared for, valued, and truly seen. We also proudly offer a new citywide one-way dual language program in Spanish, supporting multiliteracy and multicultural development. This initiative enriches our student educational journey by promoting bilingualism and fostering a deeper understanding of diverse cultures. We are dedicated to providing opportunities that encourage collaboration between our UNMS community members, because we know it takes a village to educate the whole child. Together, we make the difference!

overview: Our mission at Urban Assembly Academy for Future Leaders (AFL) is to welcome learners who have broad intellectual interests. We encourage our scholars to develop their wide spectrum of knowledge. Rather than limiting students' adolescent curiosity by having them specialize in one academic area, AFL supports our scholars' intense desire to know and understand. At AFL, we foster an environment that promotes adolescent development and demands academic excellence. Though we are a very small school, we offer our students an abundance of professional opportunities and experiences. Our students travel and get real-life experience to support what they are learning in class. Students at AFL can take advantage of our top-ranked athletic program; science, technology and arts-based elective courses; and advisory program. We challenge, support, and expose our students to the ways in which highly successful people think, so that throughout their three years at AFL they may hone their skills and leave our doors ready to lead the world.

overview: At The Urban Assembly Institute of Math and Science for Young Women (UAI), girls and gender-expansive youth are leading the way in STEMand now exploring the future of healthcare and education, too! Located in Downtown Brooklyn, UAI is a public all-girls school where students thrive in a safe, supportive, and inspiring environment. Our strong student-teacher relationships and rigorous college-preparatory curriculum help students achieve at high levels, with many taking high school Regents exams in math, science, and history by 8th grade. Learning comes alive through hands-on projects, field trips, and real-world experiences that spark curiosity and confidence. We’re excited to offer Future Ready pathways in nursing and education, giving 8th graders early exposure to rewarding, high-demand careers. Whether students dream of becoming doctors, teachers, engineers, entrepreneurs, or something entirely their own, UAI helps them build the skills and confidence to succeed. Students also enjoy a free after-school program in partnership with Girls Inc. NYC, featuring clubs and activities that foster creativity, leadership, and personal growth. With small class sizes, dedicated educators, and a strong sense of sisterhood, UAI is more than a school- it’s a community where future leaders, innovators, and change makers grow. Join UAI and start building your future today!
